  1605	def _locked_append(
  1606	    ledger_path: Path,
  1607	    build: Any,
  1608	) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
  1609	    ledger_path = Path(ledger_path)
  1610	    ledger_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  1611	    lock_descriptor = _open_ledger_lock(ledger_path)
  1612	    try:
  1613	        fcntl.flock(lock_descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
  1614	        descriptor = os.open(
  1615	            ledger_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o600
  1616	        )
  1617	        try:
  1618	            with os.fdopen(descriptor, "r+b", closefd=False) as handle:
  1619	                handle.seek(0)
  1620	                raw = handle.read()
  1621	                receipts, reasons = _parse_ledger(raw)
  1622	                if reasons:
  1623	                    raise CalibrationLedgerError(", ".join(sorted(reasons)))
  1624	                receipt = build(receipts)
  1625	                if not _valid_receipt_shape(receipt):
  1626	                    raise CalibrationLedgerError(
  1627	                        "writer constructed a malformed receipt"
  1628	                    )
  1629	                payload = canonical_json_bytes(receipt) + b"\n"
  1630	                handle.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
  1631	                handle.write(payload)
  1632	                handle.flush()
  1633	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
  1634	                return _frozen_mapping(receipt)
  1635	        finally:
  1636	            os.close(descriptor)
  1637	    finally:
  1638	        os.close(lock_descriptor)

   431	def load_calibration_acceptance_bound(
   432	    path: Path = DEFAULT_ACCEPTANCE_BOUND_PATH,
   433	) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
   434	    """Load the file-pinned D-102 acceptance artifact fail-closed."""

   443	def _acceptance_bound_from_authenticated_bytes(
   444	    raw: bytes,
   445	) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
   446	    """Parse acceptance bytes only when their role-indexed pin authenticates."""
   447	
   448	    try:
   449	        value = json.loads(raw)
   450	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
   451	        return None
   452	    # Any file route is authenticated by one of the two reviewed exact-byte
   453	    # states: the genesis fixture retained for pre-issuance tests, or the
   454	    # deterministically emitted issued artifact. A caller cannot turn an
   455	    # alternate self-consistent document into authority by choosing a path.
   456	    expected_sha256 = {
   457	        "schema_fixture_unissued": DEFAULT_ACCEPTANCE_BOUND_SHA256,
   458	        "issued": ISSUED_ACCEPTANCE_BOUND_SHA256,
   459	    }.get(value.get("artifact_role") if isinstance(value, Mapping) else None)
   460	    if hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() != expected_sha256:
   461	        return None
   462	    if not _valid_acceptance_bound(value):
   463	        return None
   464	    return dict(value)
   465

   467	def _authenticated_explicit_acceptance_bound(
   468	    value: Mapping[str, Any],
   469	) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
   470	    """Authenticate an in-memory artifact against the checked-in byte pin."""
   471	
   472	    pinned = load_calibration_acceptance_bound()
   473	    if pinned is None or dict(value) != pinned:
   474	        return None
   475	    return pinned

   478	def _acceptance_artifact_sha256(artifact: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:
   479	    """Return the reviewed exact-byte pin for a validated artifact role."""
   480	
   481	    return (
   482	        ISSUED_ACCEPTANCE_BOUND_SHA256
   483	        if artifact.get("artifact_role") == "issued"
   484	        else DEFAULT_ACCEPTANCE_BOUND_SHA256
   485	    )

   488	def _valid_sha256(value: Any) -> bool:
   489	    return (
   490	        isinstance(value, str)
   491	        and len(value) == 64
   492	        and all(char in "0123456789abcdef" for char in value)
   493	    )

   496	def _binding_evidence_authentic(
   497	    evidence: Mapping[str, Any], bindings: Mapping[str, Any]
   498	) -> bool:
   499	    binding_evidence = evidence.get("binding_evidence")
   500	    binary = (
   501	        binding_evidence.get("powermetrics_binary")
   502	        if isinstance(binding_evidence, Mapping)
   503	        else None
   504	    )
   505	    power_policy = (
   506	        binding_evidence.get("power_policy")
   507	        if isinstance(binding_evidence, Mapping)
   508	        else None
   509	    )
   510	    # Canonical form MUST match the generation (powermetrics_fiducial) and
   511	    # reduce-side consumers byte-for-byte: ensure_ascii=False (delta-review
   512	    # P2 — the ASCII-default form made authentic non-ASCII binding vectors
   513	    # unmatchable as bracket candidates).
   514	    canonical = json.dumps(
   515	        dict(bindings),
   516	        sort_keys=True,
   517	        separators=(",", ":"),
   518	        ensure_ascii=False,
   519	        allow_nan=False,
   520	    ).encode("utf-8")
   521	    return bool(
   522	        isinstance(binding_evidence, Mapping)
   523	        and binding_evidence.get("schema_version")
   524	        == "joulewise.instrument_binding_evidence.v1"
   525	        and binding_evidence.get("binding_vector_sha256")
   526	        == hashlib.sha256(canonical).hexdigest()
   527	        and isinstance(binary, Mapping)
   528	        and binary.get("sha256") == bindings.get("powermetrics_sha256")
   529	        and isinstance(binary.get("path"), str)
   530	        and bool(binary.get("path"))
   531	        and isinstance(power_policy, Mapping)
   532	        and power_policy.get("id") == bindings.get("power_policy")
   533	    )

   536	def load_calibration_candidate(

   539	    """Authenticate one standalone validation directory from primary bytes."""

   574	        evidence = json.loads(evidence_raw)
   575	    except (KeyError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
   576	        return None
   577	    if not isinstance(evidence, Mapping):

   579	    protocol_id = evidence.get("protocol_id")
   580	    bindings = evidence.get("bindings")
   581	    capture = evidence.get(CAPTURE_TIME_FIELD)
   582	    if (

   585	        or manifest.get("protocol_id") != protocol_id
   586	        or manifest.get("pulse_count") != protocol_pulse_count(str(protocol_id))

   591	        or bindings.get("protocol_sha256") != protocol_sha256(str(protocol_id))
   592	        or evidence.get("pulse_count") != protocol_pulse_count(str(protocol_id))
   593	        or evidence.get("anchor_method_version")
   594	        != "powermetrics_native_second_censored_intersection_v1"

   596	        or not isinstance(

   685	        or candidate.evidence_sha256
   686	        != observation.artifact_sha256.get("instrument_evidence.json")

./docs/process_traces/2026-08-03-calbracket-b1-gate/inputs/streamB-fix-prompt.md:8:B2 (blocker, R2.3/R2.6) — content-bearing `abandoned` receipts are accepted as classifiable (validate_powermetrics_fiducial.py:372, calibration_ledger.py:303, :715, calibration_bracketing.py:884) though the R2 prior-set schema cannot represent `abandoned`. Fix per R2.6: `abandoned` is an UNRESOLVED class — a new abandoned observation (content-bearing or not) causes trigger evaluation to REFUSE until dispositioned; it never silently passes and never counts as classifiable. Align the finalization path so an abandoned receipt with content hashes is representable as unresolved evidence, not dropped. Regression: the audit's probe — a new content-bearing abandoned observation beside an otherwise valid bracket must produce refusal, not status=passed (red pre-fix).

    99	def _sysctl_identity(name: str) -> str:
   100	    """Read a reservation-time macOS identity before capture begins."""

   106	        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,

   125	    """Best-effort bounded termination for a calibration sampler."""

   135	def wait_for_preworkload_rollover(
   136	    capture_path: Path,
   137	    process: subprocess.Popen,
   138	    *,
   139	    timeout_s: float = 15.0,
   140	    poll_s: float = 0.05,
   141	) -> None:
   142	    """Require an advancing native plist timestamp before any workload.
   143	
   144	    Timeout is a governed refusal, not permission to fall through. The
   145	    sampler is terminated here so callers cannot accidentally continue with
   146	    baseline, warmup, or pulse work after the gate fails.
   147	    """
   148	
   149	    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_s
   150	    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
   151	        try:
   152	            records = parse_powermetrics_records(capture_path.read_bytes())
   153	        except (OSError, ValueError):
   154	            records = []
   155	        stamps = [
   156	            float(record.metadata["plist_timestamp_s"])
   157	            for record in records
   158	        ]
   159	        if any(later > earlier for earlier, later in zip(stamps, stamps[1:])):
   160	            return
   161	        time.sleep(poll_s)
   162	    _terminate_powermetrics(process)
   163	    raise RuntimeError(ROLLOVER_GATE_TIMEOUT_REASON)

   166	def trim_trace_after_warmups(

   176	    measured edge, and any genuinely uncommanded plateau after that edge is
   177	    still detected.

   362	
   363	### If a single member still fails the anchor
   364	
   365	Stabilization lowers the rate; it does not make the failure impossible. When
   366	one member refuses with `wall_minus_monotonic_span_exceeded`, no member-level
   367	anchor retry is adopted. Under D-113 clause 9, no such retry occurs without a
   368	prospective ruling made before the plan freeze:
   369	
   370	- [ ] **Do not mint a bound, a verdict, or a floor from a basis that contains
   371	  the invalid occurrence.** An invalid member never becomes a valid one.
   372	- [ ] Preserve and quarantine the invalid member. Valid members already
   373	  collected stay exactly where they are, but no replacement member is
   374	  collected under an unruled retry.
   375	- [ ] Stop the stage under the existing `--max-failures 1` behavior and take
   376	  the disposition to the lead. Do not hand-retry, supersede, or rerun the
   377	  dual-family bound mint as if a member-level retry were licensed.
   378	
   379	`--max-failures` stays at 1. Every admission gate, every family screen, and
   380	every refusal stays exactly as written. Calibration-only retry remains
   381	governed as written in §6 and is not changed by this member-level prohibition.
   382	
   383	## 5B. Pre-flight calibration screen (D-079 clause 3)
   384	
   385	**What this catches, in plain language.** The pre-calibration measures how
   386	badly the power instrument can be wrong about *when* energy was used. It
   387	reduces to one number, the fiducial bound (`b_fiducial_s` in
   388	`instrument_evidence.json`). Most captures land near 27 ms. Occasionally the
   389	GPU is still ramping its clock and voltage up through low-frequency states
   390	while the calibration pulses run — the raw evidence shows the GPU is not
   391	idle — and the estimator, which fits each pulse as a clean rectangle with a
   392	movable start time, absorbs that ramp as an apparent shift in the pulse's
   393	start. The result is an out-of-family calibration. Window B on 2026-07-26 hit
   394	exactly this: a 35.435841 ms pre-calibration, the highest in the entire
   395	corpus, which was only discovered at the post-calibration and cost the whole
   396	3.5-hour campaign. The condition cannot be predicted before a calibration is
   397	taken, but a four-minute calibration detects it reliably. That asymmetry is
   398	the entire point of this step.
   399	
   400	**The screen.** Immediately after the pre-calibration mints, and before any
   401	member is collected:
   402	
   403	1. Read `b_fiducial_s` from the newly minted
   404	   `RUNS_ROOT/instrument_validation/<id>/instrument_evidence.json`.
   405	2. Require `b_fiducial_s <= 0.033558756679900` (33.558756680 ms). This is the
   406	   larger, and so the more conservative, of the prior observed maximum
   407	   (33.558756680 ms) and the 95% Student-t upper level for a new observation
   408	   over the same n=19 corpus (33.353749299 ms).
   409	3. If the value exceeds the threshold, **abort before member 1** and go to
   410	   the retry rules below. Do not proceed and hope the post-calibration
   411	   agrees; it will not save the window, and every member collected after a
   412	   failing pre-calibration is wasted quiet time.
   413	4. If the value passes, continue the chain unchanged.
   414	
   415	The chain in §6 performs steps 1–3 automatically, so the operator still never
   416	inspects logs mid-run. The threshold is a derived, provenance-bound number,
   417	not a house style: it is valid only for Mac15,9 / macOS 25F84 /
   418	`ac_high_power` / 100 ms cadence / `joint_loss_sublevel_interval_branch_v2`
   419	bindings, and it is re-derived when any of those change (D-079 clause 3).
   420	
   421	This screen is a **level** check on one calibration, and is entirely separate
   422	from the **drift** check between the two calibrations in §8. A level failure
   423	is an out-of-family systematic condition and is never budgeted (D-079
   424	clause 2).
   425	
   426	**Retry rules — the cause-removal test.**
   427	
   428	- A failing pre-calibration ends **that attempt**, not necessarily the night.
   429	- A retry is permitted **only** when a specific, named cause has been
   430	  identified **and removed**. Record the retry as a deviation in the
   431	  close-out, preserve both attempts as immutable evidence, and stay inside
   432	  the retry count pre-registered in the frozen plan.
   433	- **With no identifiable cause, the window ends.** Stop, preserve everything,
   434	  and take the disposition to the lead.
   435	- The line that matters: re-running until the number passes is selection on
   436	  the **outcome**. That is calibration shopping, it makes the accepted
   437	  calibration the luckiest draw rather than a representative one, and it
   438	  would invalidate every claim built on the window. Re-running after removing
   439	  a named **cause** is legitimate, because the second attempt measures a
   440	  genuinely different machine state.
   441	- Worked example (2026-07-27, window C): Apple's XProtect malware scanner was
   442	  observed at 94% CPU as the window's first member began. The environment
   443	  gate refused the member — correctly. The scanner was identified as the
   444	  cause, the operator waited 14 minutes for it to finish, and the relaunched
   445	  window collected 59/59 clean. Named cause, removed, verified, recorded:
   446	  that is a legitimate retry. "It failed, so I ran it again" is not.
   447	
   448	D-079 defines this screen on the pre-calibration only. If the **post**
   449	calibration's level exceeds the same threshold, the members are already
   450	collected and no retry can help: preserve everything, record it in the
   451	close-out, do not budget the excess (D-079 clause 2), and refer the
   452	disposition to the lead.
   453	
   454	## 6. The foreground measurement chain
   455	
   456	Save the following as `WINDOW_PLAN_ROOT/window-chain.zsh`, review it, and
   457	record its SHA-256 before closing all agents:
   458	
   459	```zsh
   460	#!/bin/zsh
   461	set -euo pipefail
   462	
   463	WINDOW_PLAN_ROOT="$1"
   464	source "$WINDOW_PLAN_ROOT/window.env"
   465	
   466	REPO=/Users/edr/code/JouleWise

   478	mkdir -p \
   479	  "$RUNS_ROOT/instrument_validation" \
   480	  "$BOUND_RUNS_ROOT" \
   481	  "$OPERATOR_LOG_ROOT" \
   482	  "$QUARANTINE_ROOT"
   483	
   484	timestamp() {
   485	  TZ=UTC date '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'
   486	}
   487	
   488	settle() {
   489	  /bin/sleep "$SETTLE_S"
   490	}
   491	
   492	quarantine_stale_lock() {
   493	  local root="$1"
   494	  local lock="$root/campaign.lock"
   495	  [ ! -e "$lock" ] && return 0
   496	
   497	  local pid
   498	  pid="$(/usr/bin/sed -n 's/^pid=\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p' "$lock")"
   499	  if [ -z "$pid" ]; then
   500	    echo "Unreadable campaign lock: $lock" >&2
   501	    return 1
   502	  fi
   503	  if /bin/kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
   504	    echo "Live campaign PID $pid owns $lock" >&2
   505	    return 1
   506	  fi
   507	
   508	  /bin/mv "$lock" \
   509	    "$QUARANTINE_ROOT/$(basename "$root").campaign.lock.$(TZ=UTC date '+%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ')"
   510	}
   511	
   512	latest_calibration() {
   513	  /usr/bin/find "$RUNS_ROOT/instrument_validation" \
   514	    -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -print |
   515	    /usr/bin/sort |
   516	    /usr/bin/tail -n 1

   518	
   519	arm_for_calibration() {
   520	  echo "$(timestamp) calibration display arm: 20-second countdown" \
   521	    >> "$OPERATOR_LOG_ROOT/window-chain.log"
   522	  /bin/sleep 20
   523	  /usr/bin/pmset displaysleepnow \

   525	  /bin/sleep 5
   526	}
   527	
   528	calibrate_once() {
   529	  local label="$1"
   530	  arm_for_calibration
   531	  "$PY" "$REPO/scripts/validate_powermetrics_fiducial.py" \
   532	    --allow-live \

   534	    --power-policy "$POWER_POLICY" \

   536	}
   537	
   538	calibrate_with_clock_retry() {
   539	  local label="$1"
   540	  local before candidate rc reasons
   541	
   542	  settle
   543	  before="$(latest_calibration)"
   544	  set +e
   545	  calibrate_once "$label"
   546	  rc=$?
   547	  set -e
   548	  candidate="$(latest_calibration)"
   549	
   550	  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$candidate" ] && [ "$candidate" != "$before" ]; then
   551	    print -r -- "$candidate"
   552	    return 0
   553	  fi
   554	
   555	  [ -n "$candidate" ] || return 1
   556	  reasons="$(/usr/bin/jq -r '.reasons[]?' \
   557	    "$candidate/instrument_evidence.json" | /usr/bin/sort -u)"
   558	  if [ "$reasons" != "clock_anchor_unresolved" ]; then
   559	    echo "$label calibration failed: $reasons" >&2

   562	
   563	  settle
   564	  before="$candidate"
   565	  set +e
   566	  calibrate_once "${label}-retry"
   567	  rc=$?
   568	  set -e
   569	  candidate="$(latest_calibration)"
   570	  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$candidate" ] && [ "$candidate" != "$before" ] || return 1
   571	  print -r -- "$candidate"
   572	}
   573	
   574	# D-079 clause 3: pre-flight calibration screen. Refuses an out-of-family
   575	# pre-calibration before any member is collected. Threshold is bindings-bound

   577	PRE_CAL_FIDUCIAL_MAX_S=0.033558756679900
   578	
   579	screen_pre_calibration() {
   580	  local dir="$1"

   582	
   583	  b="$(/usr/bin/jq -r '.b_fiducial_s // empty' \

   585	  if [ -z "$b" ]; then
   586	    echo "pre-calibration has no fiducial bound: $dir" >&2

   588	  fi
   589	  echo "$(timestamp) pre_calibration_fiducial_s=$b" \

   591	  if (( b > PRE_CAL_FIDUCIAL_MAX_S )); then

   593	    echo "$(timestamp) pre_calibration_screen=failed" \
   594	      >> "$OPERATOR_LOG_ROOT/window-chain.log"
   595	    return 1
   596	  fi
   597	  echo "$(timestamp) pre_calibration_screen=passed" \
   598	    >> "$OPERATOR_LOG_ROOT/window-chain.log"
   599	}

   625	run_stage_list() {

   635	cd "$REPO"

   637	
   638	PRE_CAL_DIR="$(calibrate_with_clock_retry pre)"

   644	# The reference corpus and bound are minted inside this same quiet window.
   645	run_stage "$BOUND_RUNS_ROOT" "$BOUND_LOG" "$BOUND_CONFIG_ROOT" "$PRE_CAL_DIR" \

   647

   672	
   673	After every agent is closed, launch exactly once:
   674	
   675	```sh
   676	caffeinate -is /bin/zsh "$WINDOW_PLAN_ROOT/window-chain.zsh" "$WINDOW_PLAN_ROOT"
   677	```
   678	
   679	Expected visible behavior: each stage pauses for the 180-second settle, prints
   680	a 20-second arming countdown, sleeps the display, re-probes the governed
   681	environment, and then begins members. The two calibrations use their own
   682	20-second transient display arm. Do not wake the display to check progress.
   683	
   684	## 7. Display and screen governance
   685	
   686	The production policy requires AC power, an externally connected source,
   687	low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, the screensaver disengaged,
   688	and Nominal thermal pressure.
   689	
   690	`--arm-quiet-mode` is intentionally repeated for every campaign invocation.
   691	It is not redundant: every invocation gets a new enforcing preflight after
   692	the previous stage's process churn. The controller also records governed
   693	environment evidence and observes the display after capture. If the display
   694	wakes or the screensaver engages, the correct outcome is refusal or loss of
   695	the affected member.
   696	
   697	Do not work around an environment failure with `--environment-override`.
   698	That option records an override and makes every resulting member universally
   699	claim-ineligible.
   700	
   701	## 8. Check the fresh bound and calibration bracket
   702	
   703	After `measurement_complete`, wake the display once.
   704	
   705	- [ ] Confirm the pre and post artifacts are valid protocol v3.
   706	- [ ] Confirm pre is at or before the first claim member and post is at or
   707	  after the last.
   708	- [ ] Confirm both are under
   709	  `RUNS_ROOT/instrument_validation/`.
   710	- [ ] Confirm both are within 24 hours and share the same power-policy and
   711	  instrument bindings.
   712	- [ ] Confirm bracket-bound drift against the **derived** screen of
   713	  `0.010818 s` (10.817749309 ms), not the old underived `0.010 s`
   714	  constant (D-079 clause 1). Drift within the screen passes clean.
   715	- [ ] If drift is slightly above the screen, the window is **not**
   716	  discarded: the excess becomes an added uncertainty term carried into
   717	  every floor and claim the window produces, so the floor publishes wider.
   718	  Do not compute or apply that allowance by hand — the governed verdict and
   719	  extraction own it, exactly as they own the NEG-8 drift allowances.
   720	- [ ] Confirm the excess being budgeted is ordinary repeatability scatter and
   721	  **not** a known systematic defect (D-079 clause 2). A budget may never
   722	  absorb a measurement already known to be wrong for an identified reason;
   723	  that would launder the defect into a respectable-looking interval. In
   724	  particular, a pre-calibration that failed the §5B level screen is never
   725	  budgetable, and its window is not claim-bearing — window B (2026-07-26,
   726	  drift 11.581436 ms on a 35.435841 ms pre-calibration) is the standing
   727	  example, and `instrument_calibration_mismatch` is the correct verdict for
   728	  it.
   729	- [ ] Confirm the bound artifact was minted during this window from all 12
   730	  members in `BOUND_RUNS_ROOT`.
   731	- [ ] Confirm the bound freshness block says `max_age_s: 86400` and matches
   732	  the claim members' OS build, supply identity, and calibration identity.
   733	
   734	Do not hand-calculate or patch a family bound or allowance. The governed
   735	verdict computes both family screens and both allowances.
   736	
   737	## 9. Emit exactly one whole-window verdict
   738	
   739	Run the verdict only after the post calibration and fresh bound are ready:
   740	
   741	```sh
   742	.venv/bin/python scripts/run_campaign.py \
   743	  --whole-window-verdict \
   744	  --runs-dir "$RUNS_ROOT" \
   745	  --log "$RUNS_ROOT/campaign_log.jsonl" \
   746	  --campaign-policy configs/campaign_policies/quiet_mac_p2_production.json \
   747	  --neg8-drift-bound "$BOUND_RUNS_ROOT/neg8-drift-bound.json"
   748	```
   749	
   750	Add `--waivers "$WINDOW_PLAN_ROOT/waivers.json"` only when the frozen basis
   751	contains a waiver that the current contract permits. A waiver makes the
   752	whole-window verdict `flagged`; claim-bearing extraction requires `passed`.
   753	
   754	- [ ] Require `status: passed`.
   755	- [ ] Record `evaluation_basis.sha256`, the exact member-occurrence set, the
   756	  calibration bracket, and policy SHA-256.
   757	- [ ] Require both `gross_energy` and `idle_subtracted_energy` screens to
   758	  pass.
   759	- [ ] Require both authenticated entries under `drift_allowances`.
   760	- [ ] Confirm every member's CPU admission is `admitted`.
   761	- [ ] Confirm adapter wattage continuity is `stable`.
   762	- [ ] Treat the gross corner statistic as diagnostic, not gating.
   763	- [ ] Do not append a semantically different verdict for the same basis.
   764	
   765	A passing screen is not a declaration of zero drift. The allowance is the
   766	budget carried into every matching floor or claim envelope.
   767	
   768	### D-100 §9 amendment — explicit salvage-dangler verdict dispatch
   769	
   770	The ordinary command above never consumes a terminally absent member and
   771	never selects a salvage row. A D-100 re-evaluation is a separate, licensed
   772	operation performed only after an audited `joulewise.salvage_closure.v1` and
   773	an exhaustive `joulewise.whole_window_membership_binding.v1` have been
   774	lead-verified. It appends one new row; it does not edit a failed row:
   775	
   776	```sh
   777	.venv/bin/python scripts/run_campaign.py \
   778	  --whole-window-verdict \
   779	  --runs-dir "$RUNS_ROOT" \
   780	  --log "$RUNS_ROOT/campaign_log.jsonl" \
   781	  --campaign-policy configs/campaign_policies/quiet_mac_p2_production.json \
   782	  --neg8-drift-bound "$BOUND_RUNS_ROOT/neg8-drift-bound.json" \
   783	  --consumption-semantics-id salvage_dangler_exclusion_v1 \
   784	  --window-membership-binding "$WINDOW_PLAN_ROOT/window-membership-binding.json" \
   785	  --salvage-closure "$CUSTODY_ROOT/salvage-closure.json"
   786	```
   787	
   788	The new basis consumes every surviving member under authenticated
   789	max-bracket re-derivation plus exactly one D-100 exclusion. Every downstream
   790	consumer must name both `salvage_dangler_exclusion_v1` and that row's exact
   791	64-hex `evaluation_basis.sha256`. `--waivers` is forbidden in this mode.
   792	Creating the artifacts or running this command does not itself license a
   793	historical window; that remains a separate lead-controlled step.
   794	
   795	## 10. Failure playbook
   796	
   797	| Symptom or refusal | Meaning | Required action |
   798	|---|---|---|
   799	| Display awake, screensaver engaged, `environment_admission_failed`, or CPU admission failure | The measurement environment was contaminated or unknown. | Lose the affected member. Stop the stage, remove the cause, settle 180 seconds, and rerun into a clean slot. Never waive admission. |
   800	| `clock_anchor_unresolved` on calibration | The calibration capture could not be causally anchored. | Preserve it, settle, and retry once into a new validation directory. Abort after the second failure or any different calibration reason. |
   801	| `pulse_calibration_rollover_gate_timeout` | Native powermetrics time did not advance before the pulse train. | Abort calibration and preserve the evidence. Repair machine state outside the window. |
   802	| Pre-calibration fiducial above `0.033558756679900` (chain aborts before member 1) | The pre-calibration is out of family — typically a GPU clock/voltage ramp aliased into the fitted pulse start (D-079 clause 3). | Do not collect. Retry only after naming and removing a specific cause, within the pre-registered retry count, recording both attempts as evidence (§5B). With no identifiable cause, end the window. Never re-run merely to obtain a passing number. |
   803	| Bracket drift above `0.010818 s` (D-079 derived screen) | Either ordinary repeatability scatter slightly over the screen, or an out-of-family systematic. | If the pre-calibration passed the §5B level screen, the window survives: the excess is carried by the governed extraction as an added uncertainty term and floors publish wider. If the §5B level screen failed, the excess is not budgetable and the window is not claim-bearing (D-079 clause 2). Never hand-apply an allowance. |
   804	| `instrument_calibration_bracket_missing` | The claim members lack a valid causal pre/post calibration pair. | Mark the window non-claim-bearing. Never borrow a calibration from another power or machine state. |
   805	| `calibration_bracket_exceeds_minted_bound` | The post calibration's bound is larger than one or more member envelopes minted under the pre calibration. | Do not patch metadata. Re-reduce only through a governed prospective path; otherwise recollect. |
   806	| `neg8_drift_bound_underived` or `neg8_idle_sub_drift_bound_underived` | One family has no authenticated derived bound. | Collect the complete settled-reference corpus and mint the dual-family artifact. Never insert a constant or borrow the other family. |
   807	| `neg8_drift_bound_stale` | The 24-hour horizon expired, a bound identity changed, or current bindings are missing/conflicting. | Mint a new corpus and bound inside the quiet window that will use it. |
   808	| `neg8_bracket_abs_delta_exceeded` or `neg8_bracket_idle_sub_abs_delta_exceeded` | The gross or idle-subtracted point-drift screen failed. | Reject this claim basis. Preserve it and collect a shorter or better-controlled new window. |
   809	| `anchor_fallback_member_unusable` in a floor cell | A floor member used unresolved or fallback clock anchoring. | This is an unwaivable rerun trigger. Preserve the fragment, quarantine the occupied slot, rerun the exact member, and record supersession. |
   810	| `bundle_strict_invalid` from telemetry identity | The custody-bound config, metadata adapter, and summary telemetry source disagree by backend class. | Stop. Do not choose the convenient label. Repair custody or recollect the bundle. |
   811	| `mock_telemetry_claim_ineligible` | A custody-bound config identifies mock telemetry. | Terminally refuse the member for claims. Mock data is development evidence and has no claim waiver. |
   812	| `whole_window_drift_allowance_unrecorded` | A passing basis lacks an authenticated family allowance, or a claim omitted its named allowance term. | Refuse the affected floor/claim. Never substitute zero; rerun the governed verdict/extraction path or recollect if provenance cannot be restored. |
   813	| `whole_window_campaign_membership_unresolved` | Campaign-log provenance is missing, ambiguous, duplicated, or unbound. | Repair custody or recollect. Do not replace manifest evidence with a directory scan. |
   814	| `whole_window_verdict_conflict` | Different stored verdict rows purport to govern one basis, or verdict history is malformed. | Stop. Latest-wins is forbidden; preserve the conflict and mint a genuinely new basis if needed. |
   815	| `incomplete_existing` or an occupied run ID | A failed or interrupted bundle already owns the path. | Strict-validate and preserve it, move it outside the runs root, rerun the exact config, then record supersession. |
   816	| `another campaign appears to be running` | A live process or stale `campaign.lock` owns the root. | Check the PID. Stop for a live PID. Move a dead lock to quarantine; never delete an unreadable lock blindly. |
   817	| Operator touches display, input, lid, or power | The governed state changed during the window. | Lose the active member. If supply identity changed, end the entire window and start a new root with new calibrations and a new bound. |
   818	
   819	An anchor-fallback member may be excluded by governed extraction rules when
   820	membership still satisfies policy, but for a planned floor-campaign member
   821	the operator response is still recollection. Never accept a fallback member
   822	as a zero-width floor.

   830	  "$RUNS_ROOT/$BUNDLE_ID"

   839	
   840	After the exact replacement exists and is strict-valid, record the old

   842

   848	  --runs-dir "$RUNS_ROOT" \
   849	  --log "$RUNS_ROOT/campaign_log.jsonl" \
   850	  --campaign-policy configs/campaign_policies/quiet_mac_p2_production.json

    53	def overlap_fraction(start_s: float, end_s: float, on_s: float, off_s: float) -> float:
    54	    width = end_s - start_s
    55	    if width <= 0:
    56	        return 0.0
    57	    return max(0.0, min(end_s, off_s) - max(start_s, on_s)) / width
    58	
    59	
    60	def synthetic_trace(
    61	    true_pulses: list[tuple[float, float]],
    62	    *,
    63	    start_s: float = 0.0,
    64	    end_s: float,
    65	    cadence_s: float = CADENCE_S,
    66	    jitter: bool = False,
    67	    noise_w: float = 0.03,
    68	    amplitude_w: float = AMPLITUDE_W,
    69	) -> list[TraceInterval]:
    70	    intervals: list[TraceInterval] = []
    71	    cursor = start_s
    72	    index = 0
    73	    while cursor < end_s:
    74	        width = cadence_s
    75	        if jitter:
    76	            width = cadence_s * (1.0 + 0.3 * math.sin(1.7 * index))
    77	        nxt = min(cursor + width, end_s)
    78	        frac = sum(
    79	            overlap_fraction(cursor, nxt, on_s, off_s)
    80	            for on_s, off_s in true_pulses
    81	        )
    82	        power = BASELINE_W + amplitude_w * frac + noise_w * math.sin(2.3 * index)
    83	        intervals.append(TraceInterval(start_s=cursor, end_s=nxt, power_w=power))
    84	        cursor = nxt
    85	        index += 1
    86	    return intervals

    89	def commanded(true_pulses, shift_s: float = 0.0, uncertainty_s: float = 0.0):
    90	    """Commanded pulses whose true realization is shifted by ``shift_s``."""
    91	
    92	    return [
    93	        CommandedPulse(
    94	            on_s=on_s - shift_s,
    95	            off_s=off_s - shift_s,
    96	            on_uncertainty_s=uncertainty_s,
    97	            off_uncertainty_s=uncertainty_s,
    98	        )
    99	        for on_s, off_s in true_pulses

     1	# Calibration observation ledger
     2	
     3	The canonical calibration ledger is an immutable SHA-256 receipt chain under
     4	`joulewise.calibration_observation_ledger.v1`. D-109 R1 and R2 are controlling.
     5	The ledger closes workflow omission, unregistered evidence, and rollback or
     6	stale-head consumption; it does not defend against a malicious trusted writer
     7	or an authority that rewrites both Git and the complete ledger history.
     8	
     9	Live capture remains reservation-first: a `reservation` receipt with
    10	`disposition=pending` precedes hardware state, and exactly one `finalization`
    11	receipt closes that attempt. The repository-committed head pin is independent
    12	authority over the physical ledger head. Claim evaluation requires their exact
    13	agreement and one immutable snapshot threaded through every consumer.
    14	
    15	## Historical import
    16	
    17	Historical import is the one genesis-only exception that registers already
    18	captured, hash-authenticated observations. It is not a second writer or an
    19	ordinary capture route. Version 1 has the following fixed decisions.
    20	
    21	1. **Ordering:** members are ordered by ascending `attempt_id`, then ascending
    22	   `content_id`. Attempt IDs are required to be unique; the content-ID
    23	   secondary key only makes collision diagnosis deterministic, after which a
    24	   collision refuses rather than inventing a new attempt identity.
    25	2. **Custody selection:** import authority is a reviewed, raw-byte-SHA-256-
    26	   pinned custody manifest mapping every table content ID to one exact absolute
    27	   locator. The importer uses exactly that locator; invocation roots have no
    28	   selection authority. A missing or hash-incomplete pinned copy, a locator or
    29	   governed artifact reached through a symlink, or a manifest/table content-set
    30	   mismatch refuses. Optional roots are a strict cross-check: every pinned
    31	   locator must be discovered, and the discovered hash-complete content set
    32	   must equal the manifest set. `--emit-custody-manifest` is the only place the
    33	   lexicographically smallest POSIX checkout-relative rule selects locators;
    34	   it prints review bytes and writes nothing.
    35	3. **Transaction representation:** every member has exactly two receipts,
    36	   `historical-import-v1-reservation` immediately followed by
    37	   `historical-import-v1-finalization`. There is no summary receipt. The
    38	   versioned event marker distinguishes these rows from live capture and binds
    39	   this ordering/custody contract into every receipt digest. Every reservation
    40	   also carries `historical_import_input_sha256`, whose exact
    41	   `disposition_table` and `custody_manifest` digests bind the authenticated
    42	   raw input bytes into the chain. The terminal digest therefore transitively
    43	   binds the complete ordered member set and the exact input-digest pair;
    44	   semantically identical reserialization produces a different chain.
    45	   Omitting a summary keeps the existing two-transition attempt model and
    46	   yields sequence `2 * member_count`.
    47	
    48	Consumers must not treat an import-marked finalization as a fresh post-cutoff
    49	observation or bracket endpoint. Production candidate discovery checks the
    50	marker directly, and prospective trigger subtraction uses
    51	`CalibrationLedgerSnapshot.post_cutoff_live_observations()`. At consumption,
    52	the acceptance artifact's `prior_observation_set` must exactly equal the
    53	import-marked ledger prefix at its cutoff (attempt ID, content ID,
    54	classification disposition, and epoch); any omission, addition, or live row in
    55	that prefix refuses.
    56	
    57	### Ruled disposition table
    58	
    59	The bootstrap takes dispositions only from an explicit JSON table; stored
    60	evidence `status` fields have no authority and are not consulted. The table
    61	shape is:
    62	
    63	```json
    64	{
    65	  "schema_version": "joulewise.calibration_historical_import_table.v1",
    66	  "ledger_schema": "joulewise.calibration_observation_ledger.v1",
    67	  "identity_epoch": {
    68	    "os_build": "...",
    69	    "hardware_model": "...",
    70	    "power_policy": "...",
    71	    "sampling_interval_ms": 100,
    72	    "estimator_revision": "...",
    73	    "pulse_protocol_id": "..."
    74	  },
    75	  "members": [
    76	    {
    77	      "attempt_id": "...",
    78	      "content_id": "64 lowercase hex characters",
    79	      "artifact_sha256": {
    80	        "raw/powermetrics.plist": "...",
    81	        "events.jsonl": "...",
    82	        "power_trace.csv": "...",
    83	        "instrument_evidence.json": "...",
    84	        "manifest.json": "..."
    85	      },
    86	      "disposition": "valid | systematic-invalid | ordinary-invalid"
    87	    }
    88	  ]
    89	}
    90	```
    91	
    92	The table's exact raw bytes are authenticated by required
    93	`--expected-table-sha256`, and that digest is recorded in the prepared plan and
    94	bootstrap summary. The table member order is non-authoritative. The importer
    95	requires unique attempt and content IDs, a complete five-artifact hash map, a
    96	content ID that is exactly the canonical hash of the manifest/evidence byte
    97	hashes, and one importable disposition. `abandoned`, `unresolved`, and every
    98	other disposition outside the three values above refuse.
    99	
   100	The reviewed custody manifest shape is:
   101	
   102	```json
   103	{
   104	  "schema_version": "joulewise.calibration_historical_import_custody_manifest.v1",
   105	  "ledger_schema": "joulewise.calibration_observation_ledger.v1",
   106	  "members": {
   107	    "content-id-64-lowercase-hex": "/exact/absolute/custody/locator"
   108	  }
   109	}
   110	```
   111	
   112	Its exact raw-byte digest is authenticated by required
   113	`--expected-custody-manifest-sha256` and reported in the bootstrap summary.
   114	
   115	For every manifest-pinned custody directory the importer opens contained
   116	no-follow descriptors, reads the actual bytes, recomputes all five hashes and
   117	the content ID, verifies the manifest's complete artifact table, verifies the
   118	evidence document's raw/events/trace hashes, extracts the six-field epoch and
   119	full T1 binding from the authenticated evidence, and preserves the source
   120	numeric lexemes for capture time and bound.
   121	The authenticated manifest content set must equal the table exactly. Every
   122	selected attempt ID and artifact hash must equal its table row. Any mismatch,
   123	missing member, extra member, malformed primary document, or absent
   124	hash-complete custody copy refuses.
   125	
   126	### Genesis and atomicity gates
   127	
   128	Dry-run requires:
   129	
   130	- an empty physical ledger (an absent or zero-byte file), and
   131	- a well-formed repository-committed head pin at sequence `0` with the
   132	  all-zero genesis digest.
   133	
   134	Execution requires the same genesis pin. It normally also requires an absent
   135	or empty physical ledger. Its sole nonempty exception is the idempotent
   136	durability-confirm path described below.
   137	
   138	Every ledger writer locks the dedicated adjacent
   139	`<ledger-filename>.lock` file. That lock file is created if absent and is never
   140	replaced. A writer acquires it before opening or re-opening the ledger path,
   141	and holds it through every append or replacement. The replaceable ledger inode
   142	is never the lock object, so a writer that waited during replacement cannot
   143	resume against an old, unlinked ledger inode. Both append and bootstrap open
   144	the lock through the same audited helper with `O_NOFOLLOW|O_CREAT|O_RDWR`, then
   145	`fstat` the descriptor and refuse unless it is a regular file with link count
   146	one. If the ledger exists, the lock's `(st_dev, st_ino)` must also differ from
   147	the ledger's. Symlinked locks and hardlink aliases therefore fail closed.
   148	
   149	Execution prepares and canonicalizes the entire chain in memory, obtains the
   150	stable lock, rechecks the genesis pin and physical ledger by path, and
   151	immediately re-opens all five artifacts for every member through contained
   152	no-follow descriptors. Every hash must still equal the prepared plan. It then
   153	writes and fsyncs the complete payload to a sibling staging file and atomically
   154	replaces the empty ledger. Until replacement, readers see only genesis; after
   155	replacement, readers see only the complete chain. A write, staging-file fsync,
   156	reauthentication, or replacement failure leaves zero reader-visible receipts.
   157	Process death mid-stage likewise leaves a retryable genesis ledger.
   158	
   159	`os.replace` is the transaction commit point. After replacement, the importer
   160	fsyncs the parent directory and retries that directory fsync once if it fails.
   161	If both attempts fail, the chain is **committed with durability uncertain**;
   162	it is never reported as an atomic-append failure. The CLI still emits every
   163	canonical receipt and the full summary, whose machine-readable `outcome` is
   164	`committed_durability_uncertain`, then exits `3`. The operator must rerun the
   165	identical `--execute` invocation before updating the head pin.
   166	
   167	While the committed pin remains genesis, such a rerun recomputes the complete
   168	plan from the authenticated table, manifest, and custody bytes under the same
   169	rules. Under the stable lock, it compares the physical ledger byte-for-byte
   170	with `plan.ledger_bytes`; matching bytes enter the idempotent confirm path,
   171	which re-fsyncs the parent directory without replacing or appending and emits
   172	the same receipt chain and head/input-digest summary with `outcome=committed`.
   173	Because the input-digest pair is inside the reservation bytes, reserializing
   174	either authenticated input makes this byte comparison fail. Any other nonempty
   175	ledger refuses with the ordinary empty-ledger error. Once the reviewed head
   176	pin is updated away from genesis, a further invocation refuses at the normal
   177	genesis-pin gate.
   178	
   179	The importer never writes the head pin. After execution, claim evaluation is
   180	expected to refuse until the lead has reviewed and committed the exact printed
   181	pin, preserving D-109 R1.4's anti-rollback boundary.
   182

   184	
   185	The acceptance consumer recognizes two exact-byte roles. The retained genesis

docs/reviews/2026-07-13-comprehensive-audit/register.jsonl:83:{"acceptance_evidence": "The exact R2 spend-guardrail policy text is landed; R-018 cites D-060 as ratified; an audit-close spend-snapshot receipt is attached at docs/reviews/2026-07-13-comprehensive-audit/receipts/WO-022-audit-close-spend.json with accounting recorded or explicitly accounting_unknown/estimated; canonical session inclusion is checked as manifest-corroborated known-token sessions with resume rows deduplicated and non-manifest sessions only a labeled upper bound.", "action": "[R2 RULED] Implement the ratified spend-guardrail section verbatim: SPEND GUARDRAILS (capstone benchmark bands) \u2014 provisional calibration constants; review after two completed arcs; sunset at capstone submission.\n\n1. ACCOUNTING SOURCE. Sol spend: `codex-usage` local accounting (the standing snapshot convention), corroborated by codex-run-v3 manifest `token_usage` rows where populated. The extraction window must cover the full arc \u2014 sum incremental snapshots for multi-day arcs; a single trailing-24h view is insufficient. Fable spend: estimated from local usage accounting; each snapshot names its method and price-table version. Price table v2026-07 (pinned until amended): GPT-5.6-sol $5/$30 per M in/out, cached input $0.50; Fable 5 $10/$50, cache reads $1. All figures are estimates, not billing truth, and are recorded as such. Missing data is recorded as `accounting_unknown`, never as zero.\n\n2. DENOMINATOR AND CACHED-TOKEN TREATMENT. Token bands count total tokens (cached + uncached, all directions) exactly as codex-usage reports them \u2014 cached tokens are never excluded (exclusion invites cache-heavy gaming). Dollar figures apply cached pricing honestly. Cross-family aggregate ceilings bind in combined estimated dollars, because raw cross-family token sums are not commensurable (C-028: Sol ~180x the token volume, Fable ~3.4x the cost).\n\n3. BOUNDARIES AND ATTRIBUTION. An arc = one council-log C-row, opened at its first delegated session, closed at its closeout snapshot. A work order = one WO/task id. Failed calls, retries, resumes, refuters, fix rounds, delta re-audits, lead usage, and subagents all count against the initiating WO and arc. Arcs and WOs may not be split, renamed, or reopened to reset counters.\n\n4. BANDS. Each dimension is independent. SOFT crossing = record-and-continue: flag in the spend snapshot plus a one-line justification in the council row. HARD crossing = pause-and-ask Ed before any NEW delegated work in that category; in-flight sessions finish; quiet-machine measurement is never interrupted.\n\n   | Scope | Soft | Hard |\n   |---|---|---|\n   | Sol high session | 6M tokens | 12M |\n   | Sol xhigh session | 8M | 16M |\n   | Sol ultra session | 40M | 60M |\n   | Bench-effort WO | 10M / 3 Sol sessions / ~$40 combined | 20M / 6 / ~$80 |\n   | Session-effort WO | 30M / 8 Sol sessions / ~$100 combined | 60M / 12 / ~$200 |\n   | Arc | 100M / 25 Sol sessions / ~$400 combined / 6 Sol active-hours / 2 elapsed days | 200M / 40 / ~$800 / 12 h / 4 days |\n\n   WO dollar figures are best-effort: when per-WO Fable attribution is accounting_unknown, the token/session pair binds. Ultra: at most 2 INTENDED ultra sessions per arc, each with a pre-run recorded statement of why xhigh is insufficient and what bounded subagent work it will perform; an unintended ultra is recorded as an anomaly and still counts.\n\n   Calibration anchors (recorded so recalibration stays honest): healthy xhigh \u2248 2.3\u20133.5M tokens/session (C-030 post effort-fix; C-028 average); the recorded broken state averaged ~9M. C-028 (330.6M / 59 sessions / ~$1,050 / ~17.5h) crosses every substantive arc HARD dimension \u2014 it is the anti-example. The 2026-07-13 comprehensive audit (~30 Sol sessions + ~70 Fable agents, Ed-authorized) crosses arc SOFT on session count only \u2014 the intended \"exceptional: justify and continue\" outcome.\n\n5. CHECKPOINTS (procedural; owner = the Fable lead). (a) At arc open: predeclare one accepted deliverable increment for the arc \u2014 a corpus/measurement result, analysis/figure/report increment, evaluator requirement, or cited advancement of a D-060 gate \u2014 and classify planned delegated work as deliverable-facing or process-facing (mixed sessions count as process-facing unless separately attributable). (b) Before each next delegated call: check the completed session against its tier band (a lightweight glance, not a full snapshot); no runtime killing is promised \u2014 evaluation happens on completed sessions before any resume, replacement, or new call. (c) At WO close and arc close: take the spend snapshot and evaluate all bands. One missed checkpoint blocks new process-facing delegation until reconciled.\n\n6. DELIVERABLE-PROGRESS TRIPWIRE (binds while ANY D-060 gate is unmet). If process-facing combined estimated cost exceeds 33% of arc cost OR $250 \u2014 whichever occurs first \u2014 HARD pause-and-ask Ed before further process-facing delegation. Independently, an arc that closes with process-facing spend but NO accepted deliverable increment pauses further non-exempt process work even if the 33% threshold was not crossed.\n\n7. EXCEPTIONS AND OVERRIDES. Gate-closing work is deliverable-facing by definition. Correctness-defect and data-preservation work may override the allocation tripwire but is always fully counted. Ed direction is NOT a blanket exemption (the finding's own exemplar \u2014 bridge v1/v1.1 \u2014 was Ed-directed): it is a recorded override carrying an incremental budget and an expiry, and its spend counts.\n\n8. NAMED-FAILURE BAR FOR PROCESS INNOVATION. Any NEW process layer, tool, skill, wrapper version, or contract version requires a decision-log entry citing: (a) a named recorded failure it addresses, (b) why existing controls did not cover it, (c) the smallest new layer that does, (d) its applicability predicate, (e) its marginal budget, (f) a sunset/retirement condition. Absent that entry, it is D-060 breadth and waits for the gates.\n\n9. KEEP-DEFENDER GUARANTEE. No cap consequence auto-deletes a review layer. Layers with recorded unique catches survive any cap; a cap response batches, rescopes, or seeks Ed approval \u2014 never silently drops catch-bearing gates (final-head, integration, lead-live, claim/evidence safeguards).\n\n10. MECHANISM. This policy is PROCEDURAL, not mechanical: no checker script is built now (adding process code during an overengineering correction is self-defeating; the arithmetic is a handful of numbers already recorded at existing snapshot points). Two recorded accounting discrepancies or skipped checkpoints across two arcs constitute the named failure that authorizes an executable checker with tests \u2014 via the \u00a78 bar.\n\n11. RECALIBRATION AND OWNERSHIP. Band values are calibration constants: the lead may amend SOFT values at arc close with evidence via a one-line decision-log amendment; HARD values and this section's structure are Ed-owned. Scheduled review after two completed arcs. The whole policy sunsets at capstone submission. T09 OVERRIDE TO SECTION 1: canonical session inclusion uses manifest-corroborated sessions with known token records; resume rows are deduplicated; non-manifest sessions are reported only as a labeled upper bound. T09 OVERRIDE TO SECTION 4: the 2026-07-13 audit anchor is estimated/accounting_unknown until an audit-close spend snapshot receipts it; only a receipted anchor may be used for recalibration.", "authority": "2026-07-13 comprehensive-audit charter \u00a74 adjudication; findings C2-036", "bounded_scope": ["docs/orchestration.md", "docs/risk_register.md", "docs/decision_log.md", "TASK_QUEUE.md", "RUN_STATE.md", "docs/reviews/2026-07-13-comprehensive-audit/receipts/WO-022-audit-close-spend.json (new)"], "conflict_notes": [], "court": "T09 amended", "dependencies": ["WO-019"], "effort": "bench", "finding_ids": ["C2-036"], "id": "WO-022", "lane": "[AGENT]", "nit_riders": [], "non_goals": "Do not automatically delete final-head, integration, lead-live, or claim/evidence safeguards. Keep-defender: layers with recorded unique catches survive any cap; crude caps are the failure mode.", "row_type": "work_order", "ruling": "R2 accepted; implement the ratified policy after WO-019 and before WO-031.", "state": "planned", "stream": "FABLE", "verification_command": "python3 -c 'import json,pathlib; r=json.loads(pathlib.Path(\"docs/reviews/2026-07-13-comprehensive-audit/packets/ed-rulings.json\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))[\"R2\"][\"concrete_spec\"]; o=pathlib.Path(\"docs/orchestration.md\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"); assert r in o; d=json.loads(pathlib.Path(\"docs/reviews/2026-07-13-comprehensive-audit/receipts/WO-022-audit-close-spend.json\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")); assert d.get(\"accounting_status\") in {\"recorded\",\"accounting_unknown\",\"estimated\"}; assert d.get(\"session_inclusion\") == \"manifest-corroborated-known-token-resumes-deduplicated\"' && rg -n 'D-060.*[Rr][Aa][Tt][Ii][Ff][Ii][Ee][Dd]|[Rr][Aa][Tt][Ii][Ff][Ii][Ee][Dd].*D-060' docs/risk_register.md"}

Any NEW process layer, tool, skill, wrapper version, or contract version requires a decision-log entry citing: (a) a named recorded failure it addresses, (b) why existing controls did not cover it, (c) the smallest new layer that does, (d) its applicability predicate, (e) its marginal budget, (f) a sunset/retirement condition. Layers with recorded unique catches survive any cap; a cap response batches, rescopes, or seeks Ed approval \u2014 never silently drops catch-bearing gates (final-head, integration, lead-live, claim/evidence safeguards).\n\n10. MECHANISM. This policy is PROCEDURAL, not mechanical: no checker script is built now (adding process code during an overengineering correction is self-defeating; the arithmetic is a handful of numbers already recorded at existing snapshot points). Two recorded accounting discrepancies or skipped checkpoints across two arcs constitute the named failure that authorizes an executable checker with tests \u2014 via the \u00a78 bar.\n\n11. RECALIBRATION AND OWNERSHIP. Band values are calibration constants: the lead may amend SOFT values at arc close with evidence via a one-line decision-log amendment; HARD values and this section's structure are Ed-owned. Scheduled review after two completed arcs. The whole policy sunsets at capstone submission.",

The 2M campaign spans radically different 1.5B and 122B operating regimes [phase_2_plan.md:642](/Users/edr/code/JouleWise/docs/phase_2/phase_2_plan.md:642), but there is not yet evidence that a floor measured at one stack/power/duration regime conservatively bounds the other.

docs/reviews/2026-07-08-technical-merit-review.md:73:JouleWise is an instrument-and-methodology contribution of genuine quality with one verified-unoccupied research target of real value. The audit chain, window discipline, and claim-gating stack together constitute the most rigorous measurement-integrity design in its class, and the program's two contamination catches -- one by human review before the gate existed, one by the gate's first true positive -- plus the formal self-demotion of its most quotable number show the discipline is operational, not performative. Against that: the sensors are unverified, the corpus is a demo, the claim gate has never fired beyond partial exercise on protocol, MDE arithmetic, and ladder classification, the flagship claim is currently forbidden in its strongest form by the project's own rules, and there is a concrete physical hole in the planned transfer-energy accounting on discrete-GPU ends. Published today it would be an excellent methods paper with a demonstration corpus. The distance to the strong version is short and fully enumerated by the project itself -- a wall meter, a seeded split analysis-plan row, a host-side boundary fix, floor calibration, and one campaign through the full chain -- after which the split corpus would be a first-of-kind dataset with an audit trail no peer can match. The program's merit is real; almost all of it is still ahead of the data.

impact.</li> <li>Fallback: what we do <em>if it happens</em> - every fallback must preserve a publishable result, even if smaller.</li> <li>Owner: <code>user</code> for actions needing Likelihood: medium. Impact: high (wrong deliverable built).</li> <li>Trigger: Phase 2 implementation slices ready to start (2A-2F complete) with P1-001 still open; or any supervisor communication contradicting <code>AGENT_PLAN.md</code> scope.</li> <li>Status note (2026-07-05): the first trigger fired 2026-06-12 (2A-2F completed with P1-001 still open). The mitigation is holding as designed - all work since has been hardware-independent and harness-shaped (mock slice, docs, Slice 2N is next and is also ungated) - and the fallback (&quot;continue only mock/local work; hardware purchases/borrows blocked-on-approval&quot;) is effectively in force.</li> <li>Mitigation: the queue keeps P1-001 ranked first; all work until approval stays hardware-independent and harness-shaped (valuable under any scope); the Phase 1 exit checklist lists the exact questions to put to the supervisor so one meeting can close the gate.</li> <li>Fallback: if approval stalls past mock-slice completion, continue only mock/local work and mark every hardware purchase or borrow decision blocked-on-approval.</li> <li>Owner: user.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-002-powermetrics-sudo-workflow-not-approved-on-measurement-mac">R-002: powermetrics sudo workflow not approved on measurement Mac</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2. Likelihood: low (user controls the machine; a local auth session needs rescheduling - the planned 2026-06-10 slot passed without one). Impact: high (no Mac telemetry = no flagship vertical slice).</li> <li>Status: closed-residual (2026-07-08). The working Mac slice completed 2G/2H/2I on 2026-07-06 with privileged powermetrics capture and strict-valid bundles; revisit for new macOS/MLX/powermetrics versions or new Mac hardware.</li> <li>Trigger: scoped sudoers rule (D-004) cannot be installed, or privileged sample capture fails after the auth session.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-004 defines a minimal, single-binary sudoers rule with the exact line documented in the Phase 1 exit checklist&#39;s instrumentation section; interactive-sudo manual fallback documented for attended runs.</li> <li>Fallback: attended runs with interactive sudo (operator present per experiment); if even that is unacceptable, the Mac becomes runtime-supported/telemetry-blocked and the first real slice moves to the first available CUDA target - recorded as a finding, not hidden.</li> <li>Owner: user (install rule), agent (pre-check + structured failure).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-003-mlx-install-or-model-load-failure-on-mac">R-003: MLX install or model-load failure on Mac</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2. Likelihood: low. Impact: medium (delays flagship slice).</li> <li>Status: closed-residual (2026-07-08). The working Mac slice completed 2G/2H/2I on 2026-07-06 with MLX generation and strict-valid bundles; revisit for new MLX/mlx-lm versions or new Mac hardware.</li> <li>Trigger: <code>pip install mlx mlx-lm</code> fails, or the chosen model (D-016) has no working MLX artifact.</li> <li>Mitigation: install into a dedicated venv with versions recorded in run bundles; model criteria (D-016) require known MLX availability before selection; smoke-test load before scheduling measurement sessions.</li> <li>Fallback: llama.cpp with the Metal backend as the Mac runtime (already a planned runtime for split portability under D-015); the MLX adapter then becomes optional rather than flagship.</li> <li>Owner: agent (with user approving installs).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-004-kv-persist-resume-unsupported-in-a-target-runtime">R-004: KV persist/resume unsupported in a target runtime</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium overall (high for vLLM file-based replay, low for llama.cpp, low-medium for mlx-lm). Impact: high if unmitigated - this is the project&#39;s central feasibility risk.</li> <li>Trigger: a Stage 3.0 spike returns <code>replay_unsupported</code> for a runtime needed by a planned pairing.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-015&#39;s feasibility ladder - spikes run <em>before</em> any split hardware time is scheduled; pairings are planned only on runtimes with <code>replay_supported</code> verdicts; the synthetic transfer microbenchmark (Stage 3.1) is independent of all runtime cooperation and guarantees a crossover dataset.</li> <li>Fallback: analytical composition - measured prefill energy (node A) + measured synthetic transfer energy (payload sized by the KV model) + measured decode energy (node B) bounds the split cost honestly; the report states the composition method explicitly.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-005-llama-cpp-cache-files-not-portable-across-machines-backends">R-005: llama.cpp cache files not portable across machines/backends</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium (session files are version- and model-sensitive; cross-backend CUDA-save -&gt; Metal-load is unverified). Impact: high for <em>heterogeneous</em> pairings specifically.</li> <li>Trigger: Stage 3.0.2&#39;s cross-machine restore test fails or produces divergent output.</li> <li>Mitigation: the spike tests cross-machine restore explicitly, with pinned identical llama.cpp versions and identical GGUF files on both ends, before any heterogeneous experiment is scheduled.</li> <li>Fallback: restrict offline-replay pairings to same-platform pairs (GPU-&gt;GPU in the borrow window, Orin-&gt;Orin); cover heterogeneous pairs with the analytical composition (R-004 fallback); report the portability finding itself - it is a legitimate disaggregation-practicality result.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-006-3080-ti-borrow-window-slips-or-shrinks">R-006: 3080 Ti borrow window slips or shrinks</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium (loses GPU-&gt;GPU pairing, not the phase).</li> <li>Trigger: window not scheduled by Phase 3 Stage 3.2 completion; or window arrives before split tooling is ready.</li> <li>Mitigation: all split tooling reaches rehearsed-on-available-hardware state before the window (the Phase 3 plan keeps a borrow-window runbook so borrow time is execution-only, no debugging); calendar mapping task (P1-008) makes the window a tracked date.</li> <li>Fallback: GPU-&gt;GPU pairing drops to single-GPU prefill/decode phase decomposition plus analytical composition; 3050&lt;-&gt;Orin and Orin&lt;-&gt;Orin remain.</li> <li>Owner: user (scheduling), agent (runbook readiness).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-007-no-wall-meter-available">R-007: No wall meter available</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 1-4. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium (boundary calibration and Pi/Hailo coverage lost; per-target results stand).</li> <li>Trigger: P1-003 resolves &quot;unavailable&quot;.</li> <li>Mitigation: P1-003 is a Phase 1 gate precisely so this resolves before it matters; D-018&#39;s boundary table makes results honest without a meter.</li> <li>Fallback: report within-target comparisons (always boundary-consistent) as primary; flag cross-target absolute comparisons with the boundary caveat; targets with no platform telemetry (Pi) become telemetry-unavailable findings.</li> <li>Owner: user.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-008-orin-telemetry-inaccessible">R-008: Orin telemetry inaccessible</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2-3. Likelihood: medium (rail sysfs paths vary by L4T version). Impact: low (one target of several).</li> <li>Trigger: P1-006 evidence shows neither INA3221 sysfs nor tegrastats usable.</li> <li>Mitigation: two candidate mechanisms documented before hardware time; wall-meter fallback if R-007 resolves positively.</li> <li>Fallback: Orin runs runtime-only (latency/throughput) marked telemetry-unavailable, or drops to a stretch target.</li> <li>Owner: user (access), agent (adapter).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-009-hailo-cannot-run-llm-shaped-workloads">R-009: Hailo cannot run LLM-shaped workloads</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 1. Likelihood: high. Impact: low - <em>by design</em>: the plan treats Hailo as a feasibility investigation whose negative verdict is itself a reportable applicability finding.</li> <li>Status: <strong>realized as expected, 2026-06-12</strong> — verdict <code>unsupported_workload</code>. The trigger fired (a non-<code>supported</code> verdict), the by-design mitigation held, and the outcome is the publishable applicability finding the plan anticipated. No schedule impact.</li> <li>Trigger: feasibility checklist closes with any non-<code>supported</code> verdict. (Fired 2026-06-12.)</li> <li>Mitigation: none needed; the verdict-code structure in the Phase 1 exit checklist&#39;s Hailo section makes the outcome publishable either way. Do not spend implementation effort on a Hailo backend (the verdict is now recorded; the standing do-not-do-yet rule becomes &quot;report, don&#39;t implement&quot;).</li> <li>Fallback: Pi 5 CPU-only llama.cpp with wall-meter telemetry becomes an optional low-power data point if the meter exists; otherwise Pi/Hailo appears only in the applicability table.</li> <li>Owner: user (device access), agent (verdict documentation - done).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-010-controller-as-dut-contamination-on-mac-runs">R-010: Controller-as-DUT contamination on Mac runs</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2. Likelihood: high if unmitigated. Impact: medium (biased flagship numbers).</li> <li>Status: mitigated by D-013 (idle baseline includes resident quiescent controller; deferred logging; blocking wait during measured window).</li> <li>Trigger (residual): SSH-controlled comparison runs (once transport exists) show a delta beyond run-to-run variance.</li> <li>Fallback: move Mac headline measurements to remote-controlled runs.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-011-benchmark-network-cannot-be-isolated">R-011: Benchmark network cannot be isolated</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium (campus/home network constraints unknown until P1-004 closes). Impact: medium (noisy transfer measurements).</li> <li>Trigger: P1-004 topology answer shows shared links only.</li> <li>Mitigation: prefer direct node-to-node cabling (no switch) for 1GbE/2.5GbE point-to-point tests - removes the isolation question entirely for two-node experiments; record link conditions per run in the bundle.</li> <li>Fallback: run sweeps off-hours, repeat n&gt;=5, report observed throughput alongside nominal link speed (the bundle already records measured throughput per D-008&#39;s transfer block).</li> <li>Owner: user (hardware), agent (recording).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-012-schedule-five-phases-vs-fixed-academic-deadlines">R-012: Schedule: five phases vs fixed academic deadlines</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: all. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high (capstones fail by calendar, not by code).</li> <li>Trigger: any phase exceeding its (to-be-set) calendar budget; colloquium or report dates announced (P1-008) leaving less runway than the plan assumes.</li> <li>Mitigation: P1-008 maps phases to real dates as soon as the user supplies them (<code>docs/milestones.md</code> holds the skeleton); every phase defines a hardware-independent floor and a descope ladder so cutting is a decision, not a scramble.</li> <li>Descope ladder (worst-case minimum viable capstone, in cut order):<ol> <li>Drop live split (3.3) - already stretch.</li> <li>Drop 10GbE and one model size.</li> <li>Drop heterogeneous replay pairs (keep synthetic transfer + analytical composition).</li> <li>Drop Orin/Pi targets (keep Mac + one CUDA).</li> <li>Floor: mock harness + Mac vertical slice + homogeneous baselines + synthetic interconnect sweep + analytical split model. This is still a complete, defensible benchmark-plus-study.</li> </ol> </li> <li>Owner: user (dates), agent (floor discipline).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-013-thermal-throttling-confounds-measurements">R-013: Thermal throttling confounds measurements</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2-4. Likelihood: medium (high on passively-cooled Orin/Pi). Impact: medium (rep-to-rep drift, biased late reps).</li> <li>Status: mitigated by D-014 (idle-power recovery gate between reps, thermal_drift_c in measurement quality, interleaved ordering) - residual risk on targets without thermal sensors.</li> <li>Trigger: thermal_drift_c trending across reps, or cooldown cap hits recorded in bundles.</li> <li>Fallback: longer cooldowns, active cooling notes recorded in run metadata, or excluding throttled reps <em>with documented cause</em> per D-014.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-014-model-weights-become-unavailable-or-gated">R-014: Model weights become unavailable or gated</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2+. Likelihood: low. Impact: medium (mid-project model swap breaks comparability).</li> <li>Trigger: chosen model&#39;s hub entry gated/removed; license terms change.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-016 requires mirroring chosen weights to local storage immediately on selection, with revisions and hashes recorded.</li> <li>Fallback: promote the recorded fallback candidate; re-run affected baselines (the config hash separates old/new data cleanly).</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-015-schema-changes-after-data-collection-starts">R-015: Schema changes after data collection starts</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2+. Likelihood: low. Impact: high (existing bundles unreadable or silently misread).</li> <li>Status: mitigated structurally.</li> <li>Mitigation: schema_version field exists from v0.1; D-008 plans the only anticipated breaking-shape change (v0.2) <em>before</em> split data collection; output-schema additions are additive-only (the JSON schema does not forbid additional properties); <code>validate-bundle</code> pins what a valid bundle means per version.</li> <li>Trigger: any proposed non-additive change to a schema with bundles already on disk.</li> <li>Fallback: a dated migration note in this repo plus a one-shot migration script; never edit bundles in place (they are evidence).</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-016-measurement-corpus-loss-runs-has-no-backup-path">R-016: Measurement-corpus loss (runs/ has no backup path)</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2-5. Likelihood: low. Impact: high (the dataset behind every claim is a gitignored directory on one disk; a disk failure or an errant delete erases the evidence the defense rests on, and hardware re-collection needs access windows that may not recur).</li> <li>Trigger: first real (non-mock) bundle written; any data-affecting incident (disk error, iCloud eviction anomaly, accidental delete).</li> <li>Mitigation: before the first real measurement session (gate on 2I data collection, tracked as queue task P0-002), define and record the backup protocol here: destination (external disk and/or cloud location outside the repo), cadence (after every measurement session), method (rsync of <code>runs/</code> plus experiment manifests), and a restore test performed once. Configs + manifests already make re-collection well-defined; backups make it unnecessary.</li> <li><strong>Protocol recorded (2026-07-06, P0-002 closed interim).</strong> Destination: <code>~/JouleWise-backup</code> — a user-directed INTERIM location on the same disk (&quot;cursory... I&#39;ll handle that later&quot;); it protects against errant deletes but not disk failure, so the user still owes an external/cloud destination for full mitigation. Cadence: after every measurement session. Method: <code>scripts/backup_runs.sh [RUNS_DIR] [DEST]</code> (rsync -a, never <code>--delete</code>; dated UTC log line per invocation appended to <code>DEST/backup.log</code>). Restore test performed 2026-07-06: mock bundle backed up, restored to a temp dir, <code>validate-bundle</code> green on the restored copy. Swapping in the final destination is a one-argument change (or edit the script default) plus one fresh restore test.</li> <li><strong>Protocol upgraded (2026-07-10/11, P0-003 closed; addendum 2026-07-16 closing a summary-row/body drift found by the resumption audit).</strong> The interim same-disk destination above is superseded: the external destination is iCloud Drive, live with a fresh backup + restore test passed (evidence: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-11-c028-continuation.md</code> §11, &quot;The P0-003 iCloud measurement-corpus backup and restore gate is satisfied&quot;). The 2026-07-06 entry above is retained as history. Standing caveat: iCloud eviction — re-verify the destination is materialized (fresh restore test) before each measurement window.</li> <li>Fallback: re-run affected experiments from their configs (the config hash separates old/new data cleanly per D-005/D-010); report any unrecoverable gap honestly in the exclusion log.</li> <li>Owner: user (destination/media), agent (protocol doc + restore test).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-017-repo-lives-on-icloud-synced-desktop-eperm-lock-recurrence">R-017: Repo lives on iCloud-synced Desktop (EPERM lock recurrence)</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: all. Likelihood: low (mitigated; was high while on Desktop). Impact: medium (blocks work sessions mid-run; small integrity risk around eviction during writes).</li> <li>Status: <strong>mitigated 2026-07-05</strong> - the repo moved off the synced Desktop (current canonical path: <code>~/code/JouleWise</code>; the interim <code>~/code/CapstoneRivoire/Capstone</code> path recorded here was itself later renamed - corrected 2026-07-09, C-027). P0-001 complete; git + suite verified green at the new path. Residual exposure: agent sessions launched from the stale Desktop path (delete the leftover <code>~/Desktop/CapstoneRivoire</code> husk after relaunching from the new path), and any future placement of repo or <code>runs/</code> data under an iCloud-synced directory - do not.</li> <li>Trigger: any <code>Operation not permitted</code> on read/readdir inside the repo with the iCloud file provider (<code>bird</code>) active.</li> <li>History: first incident 2026-06-12 (documented in <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>); recurred 2026-07-05 mid-run - <code>docs/</code>, <code>joulewise/</code>, <code>tests/</code>, <code>.git</code>, and the repo root EPERM-locked intermittently during an active iCloud full-sync, clearing and re-locking per subtree. Both incidents match iCloud &quot;Optimize Mac Storage&quot; behavior on <code>~/Desktop/</code>. The move landed the same day as the second incident.</li> <li>Fallback: if a lock ever strikes again, wait for it to clear (both incidents did), then re-verify with the test suite before continuing; the remote (<code>origin/main</code>) bounds code loss to the working tree.</li> <li>Owner: user (launch paths), agent (post-lock verification discipline).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-018-the-agent-loop-itself-as-a-schedule-and-scope-risk">R-018: The agent loop itself as a schedule and scope risk</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: all. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high (capstones fail by calendar, R-012).</li> <li>Registered by C-027 (NEGSPACE lens finding accepted in council): the multi-agent workflow can remain locally productive - packs, registries, meta-process, site work - while the graded deliverable path (rubric, report source, backup, real corpus, figures) stays starved. Same-day evidence at registration: ~6M tokens of breadth work vs six real corpus bundles, no report source, same-disk backup.</li> <li>Trigger: an agent-heavy work block that produces neither a new real evidence bundle nor a report/figure increment.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-060 depth-before-breadth stop line (RATIFIED by Ed 2026-07-10) extended by the WO-022/R2 spend guardrails (<code>docs/orchestration.md</code> §Spend guardrails, 2026-07-15); RPT-001 vertical slice; the C-027 correctness rows ranked ahead of all breadth work.</li> <li>Owner: lead (queue discipline + guardrail checkpoints), Ed (HARD bands and structure).</li> </ul> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/risk_register.md · commit dbd8137 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>
