Flagged for Ed&#39;s PR-gate review. Also registered (fix-round F3): <code>whole_window_drift_allowance_unrecorded</code> (passing basis-bearing verdict with no authenticated per-family allowance, or a claim missing its named allowance term — refuse, never zero; in both the floor-extraction and reducer vocabularies, mirroring <code>interpolation_bound_unrecorded</code>).</p> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum 3 — terminal mock bar (lead, 2026-07-24).</strong> The ratified premise &quot;mock telemetry can never bear claims&quot; had no terminal enforcement at the analysis claim boundary: honest mock members reached floor cells and claim evidence with the mock-exempted barriers disabled. Registered spelling: <code>mock_telemetry_claim_ineligible</code> (claim-bearing consumption of a member whose custody-bound config telemetry backend is the mock class; refuse — development-only evidence, no waiver spelling exists). Mockness derives from the custody-bound config (<code>hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bytes bound via <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>), never from summary/metadata labels alone; where such a config exists, config/metadata/summary telemetry identities must agree by backend class (governed <code>mock:*</code> tags are mock class) or the bundle is strict-invalid. Config absence is non-production evidence (fixture-only permissive paths keep their ratified intent). Lead-initiated; flagged for Ed&#39;s PR-gate review.</p> <ol start="11"> <li><strong>Attribution-limited detection floors — Ed-RATIFIED amendment (2026-07-25).</strong> The first collection under the merged SCREEN+BUDGET rules (windows a9, a10; both whole-window verdicts PASSED) could not produce a floor: all three of a10&#39;s phase-absolute cells refuse <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code>. <strong>Finding: the instrument is ATTRIBUTION-limited, not NOISE-limited.</strong> Repeatability is 0.29-0.49 J on ~50 J points (and a settled reference pair three hours apart agreed to 0.007 J), but each member carries a clock-anchor-shift envelope of ~0.7-1.0 J: a +/-31 ms window shift across a phase boundary where power swings ~33 W mis-attributes ~1 J between prefill and decode. The composed bound is additive and measured — fiducial 24.9 ms (80-87%) plus bundle-local 3.3-6.1 ms plus edge span. Because repeatability will always beat attribution here, the refusal is STRUCTURALLY PERMANENT: no future phase corpus can pass it and there is nothing to re-collect around.</li> </ol> <p> <strong>Alternatives measured and eliminated</strong> (authenticated replay, 2026-07-25): (a) the calibration-bracket gap is NOT the cause — every cell refuses under both its minted and its post-bracket bound (delta +0.167 ms); (b) instrument tightening cannot rescue it — extraction would require a 10x (decode) to 32x (prefill) bound reduction, and each cell&#39;s bundle-local term ALONE (3.3-6.1 ms) already exceeds the entire required bound (0.99-2.9 ms), so even a perfect fiducial calibration would still refuse; (c) coarser granularity does not rescue it — request-level cells replayed on a10 and a8 have smaller envelopes (1.5-1.9 J) but still dominate and still refuse; (d) an ABBA common-mode estimator gives a real 3x gain (a5 decode 6.46 J -&gt; 2.13 J) but remains above that cell&#39;s 0.60 J point floor. The labelled path below is therefore not the preferred option among several — it is the only remaining path to any detection floor at all, at any granularity, on this instrument.</p> <p> <strong>Ruling (Ed-ratified).</strong> D-054 registers the detection floor as a practical prediction bound on FALSE OBSERVED EFFECTS, not as a repeatability statistic; a false observed effect may arise from scatter OR from anchor mis-attribution, and the corner-widened maximum is exactly the largest false effect this instrument can produce. <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code> therefore becomes a LABELLED CLAIM PATH rather than a hard refusal: extraction publishes the widened floor with a <code>floor_source</code> field naming the dominant term (here <code>E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j</code>) and retains the point floor separately as the repeatability diagnostic. The gate keeps its real function — preventing a repeatability-only number from publishing as if it were the whole story — while no longer conflating &quot;unsound corpus&quot; with &quot;instrument-limited floor&quot;. a10 is sound.</p> <p> <strong>Binding condition — SINGLE-COUNT DISCIPLINE (Ed: &quot;the cost seems sensible as long as it&#39;s noted&quot;).</strong> The floor gate now contains the anchor term, and each claim&#39;s decision interval separately consumes the member&#39;s <code>E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j</code>. These are different objects (calibration false-effect bound vs claim-side measurement uncertainty) and both are legitimate, but the consequence is that the effective clearable effect is FLOOR + CLAIM-SIDE BOUND (~5 J for phase contrasts), not the floor alone. Every artifact publishing an attribution-limited floor must state this explicitly so that neither term is later removed as an apparent double count. Science must be sized to the ~5 J bar; Splitwise-class effects (tens of percent of tens of joules) clear it with margin.</p> <p> <strong>Not authorised by this amendment:</strong> any instrument-tightening program. Revisit only if a pilot shows target effects below ~3x the widened floor. The free lever is workload sizing — attribution error is approximately duration-independent while effects scale with workload, so longer prefill/decode raises effect-to-floor linearly at zero instrument cost (queue FLOOR-WORKLOAD-SIZING-01).</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <strong aria-current="page">Recent</strong> · <a href="decision_log_archive_1.html">Archive 1</a></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent. Calibration note: invited-disagreement debate briefs (steelman each option, demand failure modes + examiner view) produced markedly higher design yield than review-shaped prompts; adopt as the default shape for estimand/contract rulings.</p> <h2>C-033: NEG-8 screen+budget audit gauntlet — a new refuter pairing under A/B, four audit rounds, PR #85 (2026-07-24/25)</h2> <p>Shape: the Ed-ratified SCREEN + BUDGET wave (D-078 clause 10) was taken through four adversarial audit rounds (fresh read-only Sol per round; rounds 1–3 xhigh, round 4 high) with per-severity refuter tiers using a NEW pairing under evaluation — <strong>Opus-contract + Sol-execution distinct lenses</strong> (Ed-directed A/B; now the recorded default per the instrument-mix-authority memory). Three Sol fix rounds (xhigh, xhigh + a high alignment pass, high) plus lead bench fixes closed the findings; two lead-owned decision-log addenda were written at the bench between rounds. Commit stack on main(<code>125a48d</code>): <code>b120d07</code> wave → <code>69b65e5</code> addendum 2 → <code>ad75542</code> fix round 1 → <code>315810a</code> addendum 3 → <code>a5a7acf</code> capsule trim → <code>907ee58</code> fix round 2 → <code>dbf6339</code> fix round 3 → <code>19e15d9</code> assertion restore → <code>60b12af</code> capsule pagination → merged <code>c3e2647</code> (PR #85, 56 files, +6012/−439).</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Auditor (fresh Sol, per round):</strong> found real mechanisms in every round — round 1: estimand-dispatch downgrade (row shape selects the legacy gross-only evaluator), allowance fail-open (missing allowances silently become no allowance), anchor-gate bypass on the existing-bundle re-verdict path, and the refusal-registry gap (the authoritative registry test actually failed on <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code>); round 2: coordinated-downgrade v2 (strip basis <em>and</em> the whole drift group together) and the mock-label seam (<code>telemetry_source=&quot;mock&quot;</code> defeats both dispatch and the anchor gate); round 3: TypeError on malformed basis values, telemetry-triangle downgrade into the frozen arm at the whole-window barrier, and loss of nonempty positive-path integration coverage; round 4: two omitted assertions in the replacement companion (nonempty affected-contrast set, <code>n == 5</code>). BUT it severity-inflated repeatedly — of 7 blocker-tier claims across rounds 1–2, refuter synthesis sustained 3–4 at tier (round 3 and round 4 produced no blockers at all: three should-fix, then one).</li> <li><strong>Opus-contract refuter (unique):</strong> F2 collapse (the &quot;broken frozen replay&quot; blocker rested on a misreading of the freshness addendum&#39;s scoping — landed as a documented superseded gross-only wire, not a code fix); F6 refutation (condition-level distinctness was already contract-discharged at the consumer boundary); G1 re-price (the full-strip variant is a subclass of registered limitation L1, whose closure is queued as FLOOR-BIND-01, not a fresh blocker); G2 re-price (the ratified non-mock carve-out plus D-030&#39;s strict/raw-evidence binding bound the exposure); blast-radius refutation of the auditor&#39;s proposed G2 fixture fix (strict validation binds backend raw evidence, so the naive fix breaks legitimate fixtures); <strong>A1 terminal-mock-bar gap — the session&#39;s best catch</strong>: an <em>honest</em> mock member could reach claim evidence with all mock-exempted barriers disabled, no attacker required; the NEG-8 sentinel route on round-3 F2 (the one route with no downstream catch); and the F3 fixture-fix refutation (a production-promoted fixture cannot be strict-valid — use a patch idiom instead).</li> <li><strong>Sol-execution refuter (unique):</strong> discovery of the coordinated-downgrade <em>variants</em> (strip the drift group and restore the headline floors and the record validates clean — reproduced on the repo fixture, gate <code>20.799350577898302 → 20.399350577898304</code>, exactly the fixture&#39;s 0.4 J allowance; asymmetric removal from the comparative record alone also validates clean); the G2A adjacent blocker (the reduce layer independently trusts metadata/summary mockness in the environment and CPU-admission barriers, so fresh re-reduction reproduces the forged exemption and strict stored-vs-fresh comparison is not a backstop); identification of the authoritative mockness source (custody-bound <code>config().hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bound through <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>); the <code>mock:*</code> tagged-source class caveat (<code>axi_valid_burst</code> config <code>mock</code> vs summary <code>mock:target</code> — compare backend <em>class</em>, not raw strings); and every runnable probe, including the estimand-flip demonstration (<code>mock</code> → no refusals vs <code>powermetrics</code> → <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> on identical evidence).</li> <li><strong>Lead (unique):</strong> the two D-078 clause-10 registry addenda (2 and 3) — component-7 anchor-fallback gate ruling derived from the a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (a7&#39;s 11.85 J &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member, r03; true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J), and the terminal mock bar; severity synthesis on the split verdicts (kept F4 at blocker priority on imminent-use grounds against the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade); the capsule shard-budget trim (<code>a5a7acf</code>) and the pagination ruling that followed (deterministic <code>D-NNN</code> pagination + D-076 artifact-cap redirects); the battery-flake adjudications; and the bench fixes (registry clause, the fixture metadata line that blocked Sol&#39;s canonical run, the round-4 assertion restore).</li> </ul> <p>Rough spend (estimates, not billing truth): the gauntlet proper (audit round 1 onward) recorded 11 distinct Sol wrapper invocations — 4 audits (3 xhigh, 1 high), 2 execution refuters (both high), 3 implementation rounds (xhigh; xhigh + a high alignment pass; high), 1 capsule session (xhigh), plus retry attempts on two of them; counting the same day&#39;s pre-audit wave, fold, fold2 and run-book sessions brings the day&#39;s Sol total to ~15. Four Opus agents: three contract/design refuters (~96k / 120k / 144k tokens) plus one dictated-fills drafting/verification agent (~115k) — the latter caught five material errors in the lead&#39;s own dictation of this entry, including the effort-tier discrepancy ruled on below. Lead orchestration on top. The <code>codex-usage</code> ledger reads all zeros for the 5h and 24h windows (&quot;local quota signal unavailable in referenced session logs&quot;) — the feed is suspected broken, so no token-volume snapshot is recorded this session.</p> <p>Verdict: <strong>the Opus-contract + Sol-execution pairing changed the triage outcome in every round it ran</strong> — it collapsed one blocker outright (F2), re-priced two (G1, G2), refuted two proposed fixes before they landed (G2 fixture, F3 fixture), and produced one blocker the auditor never saw (A1 terminal mock bar). The two lenses split on G1/G2 (Sol sustained both at blocker; Opus re-priced both) and the lead synthesized rather than majority-voted, per §C-028. Adopted as the default blocker-refuter shape; memory and skills to be updated by the lead.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: on F4 the lead overrode the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade and kept blocker priority, on the grounds that the anchor-fallback replay path was about to be exercised by the next window&#39;s re-verdict. On G1/G2 the lead implemented both fixes despite the contract lens&#39;s re-price, treating the re-price as a scope argument (what is <em>newly</em> broken) rather than a licence to defer.</p> <p>Calibration note: the auditor layer&#39;s yield is real but its severity calibration is not — four consecutive rounds produced findings worth fixing while its blocker tier held at roughly half strength. The refuter tier is what converts that into correct triage; running a single-lens refuter would have inherited the inflation.</p> <p>Effort-tier ruling (lead, flagged by the drafting agent&#39;s verification pass): the execution refuters ran at <code>high</code>, not the adversarial-review skill&#39;s <code>xhigh</code> default — deliberately in round 1 (Ed&#39;s A/B spec named &quot;sol high&quot;) and carried into round 2 for comparability. The A/B verdict therefore stands on high-tier refuters, which is the STRONGER form of the result: paired distinct-lens refuters at high changed triage outcomes that single-lens xhigh refuters have historically missed. Ruling: in the paired-lens shape, <code>high</code> is the default refuter tier; reserve <code>xhigh</code> for single-refuter verification or judgment-dense standalone audits. The lead will amend the adversarial-review skill&#39;s effort note accordingly.</p> <p>Scorecard (dispositions per docs/orchestration.md): 20 findings raised across 4 audit rounds incl. refuter adjacents. Accepted-and-fixed in PR #85: 13 (r1 F1/F3/F4/F5/F7; r2 G1/G2/G3 + adjacent A1 terminal mock bar; r3 F1/F2/F3; r4 F1). Owners: all fixed items closed at merge c3e2647 (lead-verified); queued items owned by the kernel rows named above; no open finding without an owner.</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/council_log.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

<h1>JouleWise: Project Status, Plan, And Architecture</h1> <p>Audience: project advisor. This is the standalone monitoring document - it summarizes what the project is, how it is built, where it stands, and what it needs, without requiring any other file. Pointers into the repository are provided for anyone who wants the full evidence trail.</p> <ul> <li>Freshness owner: phase completion lives in the phase exit checklists; live gates and work selection live only in the generated state-kernel regions of <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> and <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code>; the canonical suite command and CI own the current verification result. This page deliberately does not duplicate volatile commit, pull-request, queue, or test-count facts.</li> <li>Repository state: <code>main</code> contains the repaired measurement instrument (D-078 phase 0) and the audited screening and uncertainty-budget rules (D-078 clause 10; council C-033). The repaired-instrument collection has 229 members across four bracketed windows, a5-a8. Those windows are useful diagnostic evidence that the instrument works, but they are not claim-bearing and do not yet publish a floor. The next step is one clean prospective quiet-machine collection following <code>docs/phase_2/window_runbook.md</code>; if it passes, it will produce the first claim-grade floors before the a8 re-verdict and Splitwise sizing.</li> <li>Project phase: see the phase exit checklists for exact completion state; live eligibility and next work come from the generated state kernel, not this reader-facing summary.</li> <li>Repository: <code>github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</code> (branch <code>main</code>)</li> <li>Live status site: <a href="https://quiet-signal-6af8833395.lakebed.app">https://quiet-signal-6af8833395.lakebed.app</a> (Lakebed capsule; it is an Ed-deployed snapshot, not the repository authority. <code>docs/site/DRIFT.md</code> records known differences; agents refresh that report when front-facing state changes and never regenerate or deploy the site.)</li> </ul> <h2 id="current-repository-view-30-second-read">Current Repository View — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The repaired instrument has completed its first collection era, but the first claim-grade floor is still ahead.</strong> The D-078 phase-0 repair fixed the timing and calibration path on 2026-07-22. Four bracketed windows then collected 229 strict members (a5-a8). They are retained as non-claim-bearing diagnostic, instrument-proving evidence: they showed that the repaired path works and exposed the remaining drift-screen problem, but they are not a published floor set.</p> <p>That problem is now resolved in the merged SCREEN+BUDGET rules (D-078 clause 10). Gross and idle-subtracted energy are screened separately; each passing window keeps a nonzero drift allowance in its uncertainty budget; the drift bound expires after 24 hours; fallback-clock members cannot support a floor; and mock evidence is identified from the bound configuration and barred from claims. The next quiet session will mint its bound inside the window and collect three start references, one midpoint reference, and three end references. The older 222-bundle floor table below remains visible as a caveated historical record, not the current measurement posture.</p> <p>AXI-SB remains <code>supported</code> for native static-batch runtime feasibility with request-scoped observability; AXI-SC is <code>unsupported_for_joulewise</code> on the pinned runtime because the required speculative-decode/MTP observability or execution surface is absent. Neither verdict is an energy result. Remote protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL, and the generated state kernel remains the work-selection authority.</p> <h3>Published Window-A floor summary</h3> <blockquote> <p><strong>CAVEAT (2026-07-19 soundness audit):</strong> a trace-time-anchor defect was found in the powermetrics evidence path (power timestamps misaligned with runtime events at the ~0.5–1 s scale). It affects the corpora behind this table; every row below is <strong>under re-adjudication</strong> and none should be cited as a promoted floor until the instrument is repaired and the rows re-extracted. Record: <code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code>.</p> </blockquote> <p>Every energy value below is a false-effect guard floor in joules on the <strong>Apple M3 Max / powermetrics SoC-rail boundary (CPU + GPU + ANE)</strong>. Gross is the D-067 headline basis; idle-subtracted values are labeled within-device secondary views. Absolute rows use repeated identical conditions; comparative rows use same-condition ABBA blocks. Each primary row uses <code>n=10</code> strict-valid bundles or ABBA blocks.</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>window / basis</th> <th align="right">absolute floor</th> <th align="right">comparative floor</th> <th align="right">computed <code>floor_gate_j</code> / disposition</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>mid request, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.527 J</td> <td align="right">0.909 J</td> <td align="right">0.909 J</td> </tr> <tr> <td>mid request, idle-subtracted — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.537 J</td> <td align="right">0.894 J</td> <td align="right">0.894 J; within-device secondary</td> </tr> <tr> <td>short request, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.052 J</td> <td align="right">—</td> <td align="right">absolute floor only</td> </tr> <tr> <td>short request, idle-subtracted — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.059 J</td> <td align="right">—</td> <td align="right">absolute floor only; within-device secondary</td> </tr> <tr> <td>prefill phase, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">1.477 J</td> <td align="right">1.739 J</td> <td align="right">1.739 J</td> </tr> <tr> <td>decode phase, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.786 J</td> <td align="right">1.027 J</td> <td align="right">1.027 J</td> </tr> <tr> <td>short-prefill stress, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.027 J</td> <td align="right">—</td> <td align="right">smoke-only; <code>not_resolvable_sample_count</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td>suite item, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.333 J</td> <td align="right">4.923 J</td> <td align="right">4.923 J; drift review required</td> </tr> <tr> <td>suite level, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">1.664 J</td> <td align="right">24.619 J</td> <td align="right">24.619 J; drift review required</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>The start/end NEG-8 reference pair is an <code>n=2</code> drift diagnostic, not a campaign floor. Its gross request energy moved by 7.659 J; the idle-subtracted within-device secondary view moved by 6.608 J (same boundary). Verified extraction: <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-floor-extraction/extraction-verified.json</code>; reader deliverable: <code>docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-17-window-a-brief.html</code>.</p> <h3>2026-07-19 re-calibration under the environment guard — PRELIMINARY</h3> <p>The caveated suite rows were re-measured in two bracketed windows under the D-077 guard: <strong>94 strict-valid bundles</strong>, all admission predicates satisfied. Reviewed readout: suite gross <strong>147.96 ± 0.39 J</strong> clean (contaminated cells were ~+30%); frozen-estimator provisional comparative floor <strong>≈ 1.13 J (~0.77%)</strong> from 5 of 10 planned ABBA blocks (~22× tighter, same estimator, than the caveated figure); long-decode <strong>83.9 mJ/output-token</strong>, matching the 07-17 decode cell to ~0.1%. That corpus was claim-ineligible on source provenance (dirty collection tree); details: <code>docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-19-recalibration-update.html</code>.</p> <p>UPDATE (2026-07-19 night): the clean re-run is done — 288 strict-valid bundles with clean source provenance (<code>runs_recal3/4/5/6_20260719/</code>) cover every planned Window-A cell except DF-TELEM at planned n, including the complete n=10 suite-ABBA comparative cell; the source provenance gate is closed. <strong>SUPERSEDING UPDATE (2026-07-19/20): a same-day soundness audit found a timing bug, and no energy number from the existing recordings will be used for claims until re-measurement.</strong> In plain terms: the power meter and the workload log time on two different clocks, and our alignment between them could be off by up to ~1 second. Energy is computed by summing meter samples inside the workload&#39;s start/stop window, so a misaligned window integrates the wrong slice of the recording — dramatic for sub-second test runs (one 0.37 s run read 0.27 J when its true consumption, plainly present in the recording, was <del>8 J), and a meaningful hidden uncertainty (</del>±10 J) even on 60-second runs. Nothing measured negative; the recordings are intact and self-consistent; long-run repeatability (~0.3% across nights) shows the platform is stable. Very short workloads are simply below this instrument&#39;s resolution and will not be claimed — by design, not workaround. The fix (align on the meter&#39;s own timestamps, attach an explicit uncertainty range to every number, calibrate end-to-end with 40 precisely-timed GPU bursts before new data) is implemented and in adversarial review. Plain-language explainer: <code>docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-20-timing-defect-explainer.md</code>; technical record: <code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code>.</p> <p><strong>REPAIR COMPLETE (2026-07-22): the instrument repair is finished and signed off.</strong> Over three days the timing defect was fixed and the whole measurement chain was hardened through nine rounds of independent adversarial review (each round tried to break the instrument; the last round found one remaining gap, recorded below). In plain terms, the instrument now: (a) knows precisely when its power readings happened relative to the model&#39;s work (the clock-alignment fix, with the alignment uncertainty — about 27 milliseconds — carried into every result as an explicit error bar); (b) proves its own calibration is genuine and fresh — a calibration recording that was tampered with, mislabeled, taken under the wrong procedure, or older than 24 hours is automatically rejected; and (c) refuses to report a result rather than report a doubtful one, in every failure case we could construct. One known limitation is recorded honestly: the file that stores the detection-floor statistics is not yet cryptographically tied back to the raw measurements it came from, so we only trust such files when our own pipeline produced them in the same verified session (a fix is queued). Live validation on the real hardware passed: the validation recording (made under the earlier 40-pulse calibration procedure) detected all 40 calibration pulses with no false detections, and a test measurement reproduced the expected physics where the old defective pipeline had been wrong by a factor of ~28. Production measurements will use the newer 59-pulse calibration procedure, which supports the stronger statistical guarantee we quote for the timing error bar. Next: a fresh calibration and re-collection of the measurement campaign under the repaired instrument. Record: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-20-p0-instrument-repair.md</code>.</p> <p><strong>COLLECTION ERA UPDATE (2026-07-24): the repaired instrument has now been proven in production.</strong> Over two nights we collected 229 clean measurements across four properly-bracketed windows. The standout result: two identical reference measurements taken three hours apart agreed to within 0.007 joules on a ~38.5 joule task — about 0.02%, which is excellent repeatability for whole-system power measurement. The windows are not yet &quot;claim-grade&quot; for one honest reason: our own stability check (comparing a reference task at each window&#39;s start and end) was found to be asking a mathematically unanswerable question, so it failed every window on a technicality while the underlying data was good. After a formal debate between the two AI models working on the project — which the reviewing model won on one substantive point — the check was redesigned and ratified: windows are now screened for anomalous drift against a limit derived from measured repeatability (instead of an arbitrary constant), and any drift observed is carried into the results&#39; error bars rather than being ignored once a window &quot;passes&quot;. Reference measurements are also being tripled at each window edge. One collection session under the new rules produces the project&#39;s first claim-grade detection-floor table, which then sizes the Splitwise replication experiments. Records: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-23-window-a-collection-arc.md</code>, decision log D-078 clauses 8-10.</p> <p><strong>SCREENING RULES BUILT, AUDITED, AND MERGED (2026-07-25; council C-033).</strong> The redesigned stability screen described above is now implemented and on main: both energy families are screened separately, every passing window carries an explicit drift allowance into its error bars, drift limits expire after 24 hours so stale calibrations cannot be reused, and a measurement whose internal clock had to be guessed can never anchor a result (that one rule alone corrected a floor that was overstated by roughly a factor of three). The code went through an unusually deep adversarial review — four independent audit rounds and three rounds of cross-examination between two different AI models — which caught and fixed several ways the new rules could have been silently bypassed. The step-by-step measurement procedure for the next collection session is written up in <code>docs/phase_2/window_runbook.md</code>. Records: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-24-screen-budget-gauntlet.md</code>, council log C-033.</p> <h3>Exploratory follow-on — not a promoted claim</h3> <p>Nine additional strict-valid, collection-usable bundles cover three repetitions each of unmatched OLMoE-1B-7B BF16, Qwen3-4B INT4, and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B INT4 configurations on the fixed five-item <code>jw_mixed_v1_sentinel</code> shape. Every bundle is claim-evidence-flagged, the model/config points differ in architecture, scale, tokenizer, and quantization, and the repetition count is below the headline protocol. The values are therefore descriptive <strong>EXPLORATORY / L1-legacy observations only</strong>.</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>unmatched configuration</th> <th align="right">mean gross suite energy — Apple M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails (CPU + GPU + ANE)</th> <th align="right">mean gross energy/generated output token — same boundary</th> <th align="right">runtime-observed output throughput</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>OLMoE-1B-7B BF16</td> <td align="right">229.028 J (227.141–231.790 J)</td> <td align="right">178.928 mJ/token (177.454–181.086 mJ/token)</td> <td align="right">122.361 tok/s (122.261–122.481 tok/s)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Qwen3-4B INT4</td> <td align="right">362.772 J (362.642–362.903 J)</td> <td align="right">283.416 mJ/token (283.314–283.518 mJ/token)</td> <td align="right">106.519 tok/s (106.470–106.545 tok/s)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Qwen3.5-122B-A10B INT4</td> <td align="right">1072.273 J (1061.722–1085.144 J)</td> <td align="right">837.713 mJ/token (829.471–847.769 mJ/token)</td> <td align="right">39.473 tok/s (39.349–39.569 tok/s)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Each bundle emitted 1,280 generated output tokens. Gross per-output-token values above are derived from the gross suite numerator; the stored <code>energy_output_token_j</code> field instead uses the idle-subtracted numerator and is retained as a labeled within-device secondary view in the full extraction. For the like-for-like suite-level gross window on the Apple M3 Max / powermetrics SoC-rail boundary, the exploratory OLMoE-versus-Qwen3-4B mean gap is 133.720 J, above the published 24.619 J suite-level gross <code>floor_gate_j</code>. That only says the descriptive gap exceeds the measurement guard: unmatched configurations, evidence flags, drift review, and the lack of a prospective contrast still prohibit efficiency or architecture claims. Every aggregate and raw repetition is bundle-cited in <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-exploratory-block/results.md</code>.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-as-of-2026-07-09-c-027-whole-project-council-review-30-second-read">Previous Update (as of 2026-07-09, C-027 whole-project council review) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The project put itself in front of a hostile examiner and corrected its own front page.</strong> A seven-lens cross-model review (new Codex model, extra-high reasoning) plus an independent final examiner audited the docs, the scientific claims, the statistics implementation, the architecture, and the operating loop itself. Verdict: the evidence discipline and instrument core are sound, but reader-facing claims had drifted from the evidence (the 1.5B per-token headline used the wrong denominator — now corrected as <strong>P2-003, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~79-90 mJ per generated output token), the D-053 contrast-CI machinery exists as binding specs but not yet as code (now owned as queue rows P2-037..P2-042 and gating Window-A interpretation), and the loop&#39;s own audit trail and the capstone-critical path (grading rubric, report skeleton, off-machine backup, one data-to-figure slice) need attention before any new breadth. All measured values above remain legacy L1 preliminary observations. Full adjudicated record: <code>docs/reviews/2026-07-09-c027-whole-project-review.md</code>.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-as-of-2026-07-09-advisor-status-cockpit-30-second-read">Previous Update (as of 2026-07-09, advisor status cockpit) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The public preview is being upgraded for live advisor observation.</strong> The project-status page remains generated from repository evidence, but Lakebed now has a narrow fail-soft live overlay contract: freshness from GitHub commit checks plus parsed current fields from <code>PROJECT_STATUS.md</code>, <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>, <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code>, and the risk register. The advisor cockpit adds live snapshot state, attention items, campaign readiness, evidence cards, and claim-ceiling panels; the Story page drops hand-authored volatile counts. The operational policy is D-051: repo markdown remains the source of truth and Lakebed never hides static provenance. Current work follows <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code>: C-019 shakedown, then P2-015 quiet calibration for Window A (the CP-5 stop card was cleared 2026-07-09).</p> <h2 id="previous-update-as-of-2026-07-08-all-four-streams-merged-30-second-read">Previous Update (as of 2026-07-08, all four streams merged) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>Everything landed.</strong> The multi-stream session merged as four PRs: P2-013 and P2-014 are closed — all 31 audit pins fixed, the suite passed with zero expected failures (current count authority is RUN_STATE.md Current Verification; the suite-build merge was 732 tests and the post-alignment state is 734), bundle provenance now records prompt/workload identities, and <code>validate-bundle --strict</code> includes the powermetrics raw-plist-to-trace gate plus the legacy additive-summary comparison. The six existing real corpus bundles pass strict read-only and unrewritten; strict proves re-derivation of the recorded evidence, not independent rerunning of the hardware session. New-era bundles must carry shape-valid provenance to pass. The Stage 3.0.1 KV spike is merged with a lead-reverified verdict of <code>replay_supported</code> (tokens identical; cache size +0.018% vs prediction) — Phase 3&#39;s central technical risk is retired on current hardware. The fixture-first 2K NVIDIA stack is merged; ALL its protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL until first live hardware contact (the live-verification checklist is ready). The independent project critique now carries a second-pass reassessment (its recommendations that became code are marked resolved; 16/17 of its checkable claims were lead-verified against file evidence): <code>docs/project_critique_review.html</code>. Next: the detection-floor calibration (P2-015) then the 2M two-model baseline campaign on a quiet machine. Reader-facing status below defers to the phase checklist matrix rows for per-item authority.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-2026-07-07-fifth-update-30-second-read">Previous Update (2026-07-07, fifth update) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The instrument grew four capabilities in one session and is now campaign-ready.</strong> <em>(Historical claim; C-027 (2026-07-09) supersedes the gating: execution is conditioned on P0-003 backup, P2-038, P2-039, and P2-015-SMOKE.)</em> Five parallel work streams landed (PRs #2-#6): (1) <strong>statistical uncertainty</strong> — every multi-repetition experiment now carries per-metric 95% confidence intervals with outlier detection and explicit below-protocol flags, re-derivable byte-identically from the raw evidence bundles (verified on a live 3-repetition run as <strong>D-014 verification workload, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> 99.19 ± 1.36 mJ/output-token); (2) <strong>contamination detection</strong> — an idle-window quality gate that mechanically flags runs taken on a non-quiet machine (it caught its first real contamination during verification); (3) <strong>deep telemetry</strong> — per-sample GPU/CPU-cluster frequency and residency forensics plus a machine-state snapshot in every bundle; (4) <strong>campaign automation</strong> — a deterministic config-matrix generator and a resumable sequential runner, so the planned two-model baseline matrix (4 workload shapes × 2 models × 5 repetitions) runs unattended. A review council also produced a hardware-tiered research agenda: 16 questions answerable on current hardware alone, 10 more behind planned gates (<code>docs/research_question_bank.md</code>). The P2-013 evidence-integrity and P2-014 provenance fixes are now complete; next Mac corpus step is the baseline matrix on a quiet machine.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-2026-07-07-fourth-update-30-second-read">Previous Update (2026-07-07, fourth update) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>A flagship-class model is now benchmarked.</strong> Qwen3.5-122B (Feb 2026 generation, 122B-parameter mixture-of-experts with 10B active, a reasoning model) ran through the identical harness and workload on the M3 Max. <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~304.0 J per 512-token request. <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~298.7 J per request and ~583 mJ per generated output token. Throughput was 46 tokens/s, and the gross-energy sample CV was 0.3% across three sequential repetitions in one warm-cache session. The earlier model recorded <strong>P2-003, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~47.2 J per request and <strong>P2-003, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~87 mJ per generated output token at 257 tok/s. <em>(Metric bases and CV wording corrected 2026-07-09, C-027.)</em> First cross-model finding: the two measured points differ in size, architecture, and quantization, so they are not a demonstrated scaling law. They are, however, consistent with the fixed-vs-marginal structure Q4 models: <strong>unsubtracted decode-window mean power — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~23.5 W for P2-003 and ~27.5 W for FLAGSHIP-001, while the bigger model&#39;s cost showed up mostly as time. Also this update: the research agenda grew to six named questions (Q4-Q6) after a multi-model review council, with a curated question bank (<code>docs/research_question_bank.md</code>) and an instrument roadmap (richer telemetry parsing, a difficulty-graded scored workload suite, and implementing the statistical-uncertainty protocol) queued.</p> <h2 id="update-ledger">Update Ledger</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>date</th> <th>label</th> <th>one-line outcome</th> <th>run-report link</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>2026-07-19</td> <td>Measurement-soundness audit (Ed-directed)</td> <td>VERDICT: unsound for claim-bearing use as recorded — trace-time-anchor defect misattributes request/phase energies (all four P0s lead-verified); metric-level prechecks already failed 238/288 request metrics; four cooldown cap hits unjoined; analysis-engine wire incompat. docs/paper/draft-v1.md:88:Drift is a slow change in the machine or measurement response over the collection window. It is measured rather than assumed away. Each prospective window includes three fixed reference runs at the start, one at the midpoint, and three at the end. Gross energy and idle-subtracted energy are treated as separate claim families (idle-subtracted energy is gross energy minus the measured idle mean power multiplied by the phase duration). For each family, the protocol derives a repeatability bound from a settled reference corpus and measures the largest excursion among the start mean, midpoint, and end mean. The allowance is
docs/paper/draft-v1.md:119:*Fail-closed* means that missing, inconsistent, stale, or contaminated evidence produces a refusal rather than an optimistic default. The collection unit is one uninterrupted two-to-four-hour window with one power state, one instrument identity, fresh calibration before and after, a fresh drift-bound corpus, and one verdict over the exact member set. Work that does not fit with at least a 20% failure margin is split prospectively into another independently calibrated window.
docs/paper/related_work_draft.md:23:For JouleWise, the detection floor combines repeatability, uncertainty about phase-boundary placement, and measured drift across the collection window. The project freezes the proposed contrast, workload, sample plan, and acceptance rules before collection; brackets measurements with references; counterbalances comparison order so gradual drift tends to cancel; and raises or refuses the floor when the observed conditions are worse than the preregistered assumptions. Run bundles are bound by cryptographic hashes, which make later changes detectable, and preserve raw power samples, runtime events, configuration, and derived summaries so a result can be recomputed rather than trusted from a table.
docs/paper/related_work_draft.md:25:Paired minimum-detectable-effect methodology supports prospective sample sizing from paired differences and a one-way “prior ratchet”: if observed variation exceeds the preregistered assumption, the detection threshold may move upward but not downward [PairedMDE]. <!-- 2026-07-30-sweep-techniques.md: Paired-MDE supplies powered sample sizing over paired differences and a preregistered prior-ratchet that can only increase the floor. --> That statistical treatment does not justify combining a worst-case timing-attribution bound as though it were independent random noise [PairedMDE]. <!-- 2026-07-30-sweep-techniques.md: Paired-MDE's root-sum-square composition applies only to independent random components and would be anti-conservative for JouleWise's systematic attribution bound. --> MLPerf's per-window uncertainty and invalid-sample accounting offer a complementary rule-based model: validity is an outcome of the recorded run, not a one-time statement about the instrument's data sheet [MLPerfPower]. <!-- 2026-07-30-sweep-techniques.md: MLPerf/SPEC reports uncertainty and invalid samples per interval and rejects windows that do not meet the run-level rules. -->

   390	while the calibration pulses run — the raw evidence shows the GPU is not
   391	idle — and the estimator, which fits each pulse as a clean rectangle with a
   392	movable start time, absorbs that ramp as an apparent shift in the pulse's
   393	start. The result is an out-of-family calibration. Window B on 2026-07-26 hit
   394	exactly this: a 35.435841 ms pre-calibration, the highest in the entire
   395	corpus, which was only discovered at the post-calibration and cost the whole
   396	3.5-hour campaign. The condition cannot be predicted before a calibration is
   397	taken, but a four-minute calibration detects it reliably. That asymmetry is
   398	the entire point of this step.
   399	
   400	**The screen.** Immediately after the pre-calibration mints, and before any
   401	member is collected:
   402	
   403	1. Read `b_fiducial_s` from the newly minted
   404	   `RUNS_ROOT/instrument_validation/<id>/instrument_evidence.json`.
   405	2. Require `b_fiducial_s <= 0.033558756679900` (33.558756680 ms). This is the
   406	   larger, and so the more conservative, of the prior observed maximum
   407	   (33.558756680 ms) and the 95% Student-t upper level for a new observation
   408	   over the same n=19 corpus (33.353749299 ms).
   409	3. If the value exceeds the threshold, **abort before member 1** and go to
   410	   the retry rules below. Do not proceed and hope the post-calibration
   411	   agrees; it will not save the window, and every member collected after a
   412	   failing pre-calibration is wasted quiet time.
   413	4. If the value passes, continue the chain unchanged.
   414	
   415	The chain in §6 performs steps 1–3 automatically, so the operator still never
   416	inspects logs mid-run. The threshold is a derived, provenance-bound number,
   417	not a house style: it is valid only for Mac15,9 / macOS 25F84 /
   418	`ac_high_power` / 100 ms cadence / `joint_loss_sublevel_interval_branch_v2`
   419	bindings, and it is re-derived when any of those change (D-079 clause 3).
   420	
   421	This screen is a **level** check on one calibration, and is entirely separate
   422	from the **drift** check between the two calibrations in §8. A level failure
   423	is an out-of-family systematic condition and is never budgeted (D-079
   424	clause 2).
   425	
   426	**Retry rules — the cause-removal test.**
   427	
   428	- A failing pre-calibration ends **that attempt**, not necessarily the night.
   429	- A retry is permitted **only** when a specific, named cause has been
   430	  identified **and removed**. Record the retry as a deviation in the
   431	  close-out, preserve both attempts as immutable evidence, and stay inside
   432	  the retry count pre-registered in the frozen plan.
   433	- **With no identifiable cause, the window ends.** Stop, preserve everything,
   434	  and take the disposition to the lead.
   435	- The line that matters: re-running until the number passes is selection on
   436	  the **outcome**. That is calibration shopping, it makes the accepted
   437	  calibration the luckiest draw rather than a representative one, and it
   438	  would invalidate every claim built on the window. Re-running after removing
   439	  a named **cause** is legitimate, because the second attempt measures a
   440	  genuinely different machine state.
   441	- Worked example (2026-07-27, window C): Apple's XProtect malware scanner was
   442	  observed at 94% CPU as the window's first member began. The environment
   443	  gate refused the member — correctly. The scanner was identified as the
   444	  cause, the operator waited 14 minutes for it to finish, and the relaunched
   445	  window collected 59/59 clean. Named cause, removed, verified, recorded:
   446	  that is a legitimate retry. "It failed, so I ran it again" is not.
   447	
   448	D-079 defines this screen on the pre-calibration only. If the **post**
   449	calibration's level exceeds the same threshold, the members are already
   450	collected and no retry can help: preserve everything, record it in the
   451	close-out, do not budget the excess (D-079 clause 2), and refer the
   452	disposition to the lead.
   453

     1	#!/bin/bash
     2	# Pre-window readiness gate (operator tool; no admin required).
     3	#
     4	# WHY THIS EXISTS
     5	#   On 2026-07-27 a measurement window failed on its FIRST member, roughly five
     6	#   minutes after launch, because Apple's XProtectRemediator malware scanner was
     7	#   running at 94% CPU. The instrument's CPU-admission gate correctly refused the
     8	#   member -- but by then the window had been launched, the display slept, and the
     9	#   operator had walked away. The failure cost the launch and required a manual
    10	#   diagnose-wait-relaunch cycle.
    11	#
    12	#   Idle-triggered macOS daemons fire in roughly the first ten minutes of a quiet
    13	#   window. That is exactly when a window launches. This script checks for them
    14	#   BEFORE launch, and can wait for them to finish.
    15	#
    16	#   This is a READINESS check, not a measurement gate. It never waives, relaxes,
    17	#   or substitutes for the campaign's own environment and CPU admission gates --
    18	#   those remain authoritative and unchanged. It only avoids launching into a
    19	#   condition those gates will refuse anyway.
    20	#
    21	# USAGE
    22	#   scripts/prewindow_check.sh                 # check once, report, exit 0/1
    23	#   scripts/prewindow_check.sh --wait          # wait until ready (default 45 min cap)
    24	#   scripts/prewindow_check.sh --wait --timeout-min 90
    25	#   scripts/prewindow_check.sh --window c      # also verify that window's runs roots are clear
    26	
    27	set -uo pipefail
    28	
    29	WAIT=0
    30	TIMEOUT_MIN=45
    31	WINDOW=""
    32	CPU_LIMIT="${CPU_LIMIT:-5.0}"        # percent, per contaminating process
    33	LOAD_LIMIT="${LOAD_LIMIT:-2.0}"      # 1-minute load average
    34	SETTLE_CHECKS=3                      # consecutive clean checks required
    35	INTERVAL_S=30
    36	
    37	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    38	  case "$1" in
    39	    --wait) WAIT=1; shift ;;
    40	    --timeout-min) TIMEOUT_MIN="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    41	    --window) WINDOW="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    42	    *) echo "usage: $0 [--wait] [--timeout-min N] [--window LETTER]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    43	  esac
    44	done
    45	
    46	bold() { printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
    47	ok()   { printf '  \033[32mOK\033[0m    %s\n' "$*"; }
    48	bad()  { printf '  \033[31mBLOCK\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
    49	warn() { printf '  \033[33mWARN\033[0m  %s\n' "$*"; }
    50	
    51	# Daemons observed or documented to contaminate a quiet window. XProtect is the
    52	# one with a confirmed incident; the rest are the same class and cheap to include.
    53	CONTAMINANTS='XProtect|mds_stores|mdworker|mdbulkimport|backupd|photoanalysisd|softwareupdated|Spotlight|mediaanalysisd'
    54	
    55	check_once() {
    56	  local blocked=0
    57	
    58	  # 1. Contaminating daemons, by actual CPU use rather than mere presence.
    59	  local busy
    60	  busy="$(ps aux | grep -iE "$CONTAMINANTS" | grep -v grep \
    61	          | awk -v lim="$CPU_LIMIT" '$3+0 > lim {printf "%s(%.1f%%) ", $11, $3}')"
    62	  if [ -n "$busy" ]; then
    63	    bad "background daemon active: $busy"
    64	    blocked=1
    65	  else
    66	    ok "no contaminating daemon above ${CPU_LIMIT}% CPU"
    67	  fi
    68	
    69	  # 2. Overall load. A high load average with no named culprit is still a reason
    70	  #    not to launch; the campaign's CPU admission would likely refuse.
    71	  local load1
    72	  load1="$(uptime | sed -n 's/.*load averages*: *\([0-9.]*\).*/\1/p')"
    73	  if awk -v l="$load1" -v m="$LOAD_LIMIT" 'BEGIN{exit !(l+0 > m)}'; then
    74	    bad "1-minute load average ${load1} exceeds ${LOAD_LIMIT}"
    75	    blocked=1
    76	  else
    77	    ok "load average ${load1}"
    78	  fi
    79	
    80	  # 3. Power. The production policy requires AC with an external supply.
    81	  if pmset -g batt 2>/dev/null | head -1 | grep -q "AC Power"; then
    82	    ok "on AC power"
    83	  else
    84	    bad "not on AC power"
    85	    blocked=1
    86	  fi
    87	
    88	  # 4. Clock pinned. Measurement windows run with automatic network time
    89	  #    disabled (see scripts/quiet_window_clock.sh); a live adjuster caused two
    90	  #    window failures on 2026-07-26.
    91	  local nt
    92	  nt="$(sudo -n systemsetup -getusingnetworktime 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*Network Time: *//p')"
    93	  if [ -z "$nt" ]; then
    94	    warn "cannot read network-time state without admin; confirm the clock is pinned"
    95	  elif [ "$nt" = "Off" ]; then
    96	    ok "automatic network time disabled (clock pinned)"
    97	  else
    98	    bad "automatic network time is On -- run scripts/quiet_window_clock.sh disable"
    99	    blocked=1
   100	  fi
   101	
   102	  # 5. Target window's runs roots must be absent. An occupied slot makes the
   103	  #    chain fail late rather than early.
   104	  if [ -n "$WINDOW" ]; then
   105	    local hits
   106	    hits="$(ls -d /Users/edr/code/JouleWise/runs_window_${WINDOW}_* 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
   107	    if [ -n "$hits" ]; then
   108	      bad "runs roots already exist for window ${WINDOW}: $hits"
   109	      blocked=1
   110	    else
   111	      ok "runs roots clear for window ${WINDOW}"
   112	    fi
   113	  fi
   114	
   115	  # 6. Disk headroom. A window writes a few GB; running out mid-campaign loses it.
   116	  local avail_gb
   117	  avail_gb="$(df -g /Users/edr/code/JouleWise | awk 'NR==2 {print $4}')"
   118	  if [ "${avail_gb:-0}" -lt 20 ]; then
   119	    bad "only ${avail_gb} GB free; a window needs several GB with headroom"
   120	    blocked=1
   121	  else
   122	    ok "${avail_gb} GB free"
   123	  fi
   124	
   125	  # 7. No agent or measurement process already running.
   126	  local procs
   127	  procs="$(ps aux | grep -E "codex exec|codex-run|run_campaign|window-chain" | grep -vc grep)"
   128	  if [ "$procs" -gt 0 ]; then
   129	    bad "$procs agent/measurement process(es) already running"
   130	    blocked=1
   131	  else
   132	    ok "no agent or measurement process running"
   133	  fi
   134	
   135	  return $blocked
   136	}
   137	
   138	bold "Pre-window readiness check — $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z')"
   139	if [ "$WAIT" -eq 0 ]; then
   140	  if check_once; then
   141	    bold ""; bold "READY."
   142	    exit 0
   143	  else
   144	    bold ""; bold "NOT READY. Fix the BLOCK lines above, or re-run with --wait."
   145	    exit 1
   146	  fi
   147	fi
   148	
   149	# --wait: require SETTLE_CHECKS consecutive clean passes, so a daemon that is
   150	# briefly between bursts does not read as finished.
   151	deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + TIMEOUT_MIN * 60 ))
   152	clean=0
   153	while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$deadline" ]; do
   154	  if check_once; then
   155	    clean=$((clean + 1))
   156	    bold "  clean check ${clean}/${SETTLE_CHECKS}"
   157	    if [ "$clean" -ge "$SETTLE_CHECKS" ]; then
   158	      bold ""; bold "READY after $(( ($(date +%s) - (deadline - TIMEOUT_MIN * 60)) / 60 )) min."
   159	      exit 0
   160	    fi
   161	  else
   162	    clean=0
   163	    bold "  not ready; re-checking in ${INTERVAL_S}s"
   164	  fi
   165	  sleep "$INTERVAL_S"
   166	done
   167	
   168	bold ""; bold "TIMED OUT after ${TIMEOUT_MIN} min without ${SETTLE_CHECKS} consecutive clean checks."
   169	bold "Do not launch. Investigate what is keeping the machine busy."
   170	exit 1

     1	# Quiet-Mac Claim-Window Run-Book
     2	
     3	**Operator:** Ed
     4	
     5	**Lane:** `[QUIET-MAC]`
     6	
     7	**Applies to:** claim-bearing Mac measurement windows after PR #85
     8	
     9	**Main authorities:** D-077, D-078, and D-079 in `docs/decision_log.md`,
    10	`docs/phase_2/detection_floor.md`,
    11	`configs/campaign_policies/quiet_mac_p2_production.json`, and
    12	`configs/campaigns/window_references/README.md`
    13	
    14	This is the practical procedure for collecting one claim window. A **claim
    15	window** is one uninterrupted measurement session whose members share one
    16	power state, one instrument identity, one fresh NEG-8 drift bound, and one
    17	whole-window verdict. A **member** is one run bundle. A **reference** is the
    18	fixed `df_rq_mid` workload used to detect and budget drift. A **drift
    19	allowance** is the nonzero uncertainty term that a passing window adds to
    20	every floor or claim in the matching energy family.
    21	
    22	Do not run this procedure while any agent session is active. The operator
    23	owns the quiet machine from the first calibration through the post
    24	calibration.
    25	
    26	## 1. Rules that do not bend
    27	
    28	- [ ] Start from reviewed, merged `main` with a clean measurement checkout.
    29	- [ ] Close Claude, Codex, browser automation, periodic monitors, and every
    30	  process that would wake or poll the machine.
    31	- [ ] Launch one foreground shell chain and wait for its one completion
    32	  event. Do not inspect logs while it runs.
    33	- [ ] Keep the approved charger, cable, wattage, and power policy unchanged.
    34	- [ ] Do not touch the keyboard, trackpad, lid, display controls, power
    35	  settings, charger, or cable during the chain.
    36	- [ ] Keep every display asleep and the screensaver disengaged throughout
    37	  each campaign invocation. An awake display is a measurement contaminant,
    38	  not an operator convenience.
    39	- [ ] Use transient display sleep only. Do not change persistent display or
    40	  screensaver preferences as part of a window.
    41	- [ ] Settle for 150–240 seconds after operator activity, stage churn, a
    42	  calibration retry, or a failed attempt. Use 180 seconds unless the frozen
    43	  plan says otherwise.
    44	- [ ] Preserve every failed, incomplete, or aborted artifact. Never delete or
    45	  overwrite evidence to make a window pass.
    46	- [ ] Quarantine an occupied retry slot outside the runs root, recollect the
    47	  exact member, and record the old occurrence with
    48	  `--record-supersession`.
    49	- [ ] Do not waive environment admission, calibration, clock, thermal,
    50	  adapter-continuity, anchor-fallback, mock-telemetry, or drift-allowance
    51	  failures.
    52	- [ ] Back up the immutable corpus before extraction.
    53	- [ ] Until FLOOR-BIND-01 closes, honour registered limitation L1: a
    54	  claim-bearing analysis may consume a floor artifact only when that artifact
    55	  was produced by the governed extraction in the same lead-controlled custody
    56	  session as **the analysis**. L1 binds extraction to analysis, not collection
    57	  to extraction — collection may happen in an earlier session — but extraction
    58	  and the analysis that consumes its floors may never be split.
    59	
    60	The practical target is one compact 2–4 hour window. If the work will not fit,
    61	split it into another independently calibrated window. A long window is not
    62	more rigorous: the a5 collection showed that a delayed end reference can be
    63	physically stale.
    64	
    65	## 2. The post-PR #85 compatibility gate is satisfied
    66	
    67	Merged main now provides all of the surfaces that the earlier draft was
    68	waiting for:
    69	
    70	- **Per-family screens and allowances.** The whole-window verdict evaluates
    71	  `gross_energy` and `idle_subtracted_energy` separately. Each family gets
    72	  its own derived repeatability bound and its own recorded drift allowance:
    73	  `max(observed start/midpoint/end excursion, derived bound)`. Passing never
    74	  turns the allowance into zero.
    75	- **Reference triplet protocol.** The governed prospective references are
    76	  under `configs/campaigns/window_references/`: three start members, one
    77	  midpoint member, and three end members. The endpoint means and standard
    78	  errors feed the screens; the midpoint catches an interior excursion.
    79	- **Bound freshness.** The governed dual-family
    80	  `joulewise.neg8_drift_bound.v1` artifact has a fixed 24-hour
    81	  (`86400 s`) horizon and exact OS-build, power-supply-identity, and
    82	  calibration-identity bindings. Expiry, an identity change, or unresolved
    83	  bindings refuse with `neg8_drift_bound_stale`.
    84	- **Anchor-fallback member gate.** A fallback-clock-anchored member cannot
    85	  supply a floor or claim cell. For floor-campaign roles it is an unwaivable
    86	  rerun trigger, reported as `anchor_fallback_member_unusable`.
    87	
    88	Therefore a new claim window may proceed. Do not fall back to the old
    89	single-start/single-end practice for new collection.
    90	
    91	Before freezing the plan, confirm the command surface:
    92	
    93	```sh
    94	.venv/bin/python scripts/run_campaign.py --help
    95	```
    96	
    97	The required options are `--arm-quiet-mode`, `--arm-countdown-s`,
    98	`--log`, `--instrument-calibration-dir`, `--instrument-power-policy`,
    99	`--derive-neg8-drift-bound`, `--neg8-drift-bound-output`,
   100	`--whole-window-verdict`, and `--neg8-drift-bound`.
   101	
   102	### Decision on the three flags missing from the draft chain
   103	
   104	The merged CLI accepts all three. They are deliberately included in every
   105	measurement-campaign invocation in this run-book:
   106	
   107	- `--arm-quiet-mode` counts down, calls `pmset displaysleepnow`, and then
   108	  performs the complete governed environment re-probe. It is the merged
   109	  enforcement surface for the display/screen-contamination lesson.
   110	- `--arm-countdown-s 20` is not syntactically required; the CLI default is
   111	  5 seconds. The proven `claim_windows.sh` used 20 seconds, and this run-book
   112	  keeps that operator margin so Ed can step away before display sleep and
   113	  re-probe.
   114	- `--log "$RUNS_ROOT/campaign_log.jsonl"` is also not syntactically required
   115	  because the same path is the default. It remains explicit so collection,
   116	  supersession, verdict, and later consumers all name the same custody log.
   117	
   118	The verdict and bound-mint modes do not measure a member, so they receive
   119	`--log` where applicable but not the display-arm flags.
   120	
   121	## 3. Time budget in plain language
   122	
   123	Budget these pieces before selecting campaign stages:
   124	
   125	| Operation | Expected time |
   126	|---|---:|
   127	| Stage settle | 180 seconds |
   128	| Display arm inside each campaign | 20-second countdown plus re-probe |
   129	| Protocol-v3 calibration | about 4 minutes; the commanded schedule alone is 196.7 seconds |
   130	| NEG-8 bound corpus | 12 ordinary reference members plus one 180-second settle |
   131	| Start references | 3 ordinary reference members plus one settle/arm |
   132	| Midpoint reference | 1 ordinary reference member plus one settle/arm |
   133	| End references | 3 ordinary reference members plus one settle/arm |
   134	| Failure margin | at least 20% of the planned window |
   135	
   136	Use the dry run and prior measured member durations to budget the ordinary
   137	members. Do not estimate them from model size alone. If the reference corpus,
   138	two calibrations, seven window references, chosen science stages, settles,
   139	and failure margin do not fit in the window, remove science stages before
   140	arming.
   141	
   142	The 24-hour freshness horizon is a ceiling, not permission to reuse
   143	yesterday's bound. For this procedure, the 12-member bound corpus must be
   144	collected and the bound must be minted **inside the same quiet window that
   145	uses it**, before the start triplet. This keeps the OS, supply, and
   146	calibration identity aligned and makes the bound causal for that window.
   147	
   148	## 4. Freeze the plan before quiet time
   149	
   150	Create one plan directory outside the runs roots:
   151	
   152	```text
   153	WINDOW_PLAN_ROOT/
   154	├── window.env
   155	├── before_midpoint_stages.txt
   156	├── after_midpoint_stages.txt
   157	├── extraction_spec.json
   158	├── waivers.json
   159	└── window-chain.zsh
   160	```
   161	
   162	Each stage-list line is one repository-relative config directory, for
   163	example:
   164	
   165	```text
   166	configs/campaigns/p2_015_floors/04_phase_prefill_abba
   167	configs/campaigns/p2_015_floors/03_request_abba
   168	```
   169	
   170	Do not put the reference directories in those lists; the chain adds the
   171	governed 3+1+3 references itself.
   172	
   173	Example `window.env`:
   174	
   175	```sh
   176	WINDOW_ID=window_a9_YYYYMMDD
   177	RUNS_ROOT=/Users/edr/code/JouleWise/runs_window_a9_YYYYMMDD
   178	BOUND_RUNS_ROOT=/Users/edr/code/JouleWise/runs_window_a9_YYYYMMDD_bound
   179	CUSTODY_ROOT=/Users/edr/JouleWise-window-custody/window_a9_YYYYMMDD
   180	BACKUP_DEST="/Users/edr/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/JouleWise-backup/window_a9_YYYYMMDD"
   180	BACKUP_DEST="/Users/edr/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/JouleWise-backup/window_a9_YYYYMMDD"
   181	POWER_POLICY=ac_high_power
   182	SETTLE_S=180
   183	```
   184	
   185	`RUNS_ROOT` holds the claim-window members and calibration bracket.
   186	`BOUND_RUNS_ROOT` holds only the 12-member settled-reference corpus used to
   187	mint this window's bound. Keep the roots separate so the corpus members do
   188	not accidentally enter the claim-window member basis.
   189

   195	- [ ] Keep quarantine, operator logs, extraction output, and the plan outside

   197	- [ ] Validate every config.

   199	- [ ] Resolve every doctor warning; do not add `--ack-config-warnings`

   202

   204

   208

   221	
   222	Repeat the dry run for the bound corpus, midpoint, end triplet, and every

   224	
   225	## 5. Machine and operator preflight
   226	
   227	- [ ] Connect the approved charger and cable. Record wattage and
   228	  `POWER_POLICY`.
   229	- [ ] Finish or pause Time Machine, software updates, indexing churn, large
   230	  downloads, and cloud uploads.
   231	- [ ] Confirm `sudo -n powermetrics` succeeds.
   232	- [ ] Perform the pre-window clock stabilization in §5A. It needs
   233	  administrator rights, so only Ed can do it and the chain cannot.
   234	- [ ] Let idle-triggered background daemons run **before** the window, not
   235	  inside it. macOS starts idle-only work — XProtect's scheduled malware scan
   236	  is the documented instance — in roughly the first 10 minutes after the
   237	  machine goes quiet. Leave the machine untouched and idle for at least 10
   238	  minutes before launching the chain. This is in addition to the 180-second
   239	  stage settle, not satisfied by it.
   240	- [ ] Confirm the chain carries the §5B pre-flight calibration screen and
   241	  that the frozen plan records the pre-registered retry bound (D-079
   242	  clause 3).
   243	- [ ] Confirm both fresh runs roots do not already contain member bundles.
   244	- [ ] Confirm the backup destination exists and has enough free space.
   245	- [ ] Close every agent and browser-automation session.
   246	- [ ] Explain the single rule to anyone nearby: do not touch the Mac until
   247	  the chain announces completion.
   248	
   249	Run the preparation probe once, read its result, and correct any failure
   250	before closing the final terminal:
   251	
   252	```sh
   253	bash scripts/quiet_mac_prep.sh
   254	```
   255	
   256	That script uses transient display sleep and does not change persistent
   257	display or screensaver settings. The campaign still arms and re-probes on
   258	every invocation; the preparation script is not a certificate for later
   259	members.
   260	
   261	An idle-triggered daemon that fires inside the window contaminates the member
   262	it lands on and will fail CPU admission. That is the gate working, not a false
   263	alarm: window a9's first bound-corpus member was lost exactly this way and was
   264	correctly caught. The response is always preserve, quarantine, supersede, then
   265	relaunch (§10). It is never a waiver and never `--environment-override`.
   266	
   267	## 5A. Pre-window clock stabilization (administrator step; Ed performs it)
   268	
   269	**This is operational stabilization, not a protocol waiver.** The 5 ms
   270	wall-versus-monotonic anchor ceiling stays exactly where it is. It is never
   271	relaxed, widened, or waived, and a member that trips it is still lost. The
   272	steps below reduce how often the machine trips it. They do not change what
   273	trips it.
   274	
   275	### What went wrong, in plain language
   276	
   277	Every measured member must be anchored causally in time. The anchor check
   278	compares two clocks: the **wall clock**, which is the machine's idea of the
   279	current date and time and which network time synchronisation adjusts, and the
   280	**monotonic clock**, a counter that only ever counts forward and is never
   281	adjusted. The difference between them must stay within `5 ms`
   282	(`MAX_WALL_MINUS_MONOTONIC_SPAN_S`, `joulewise/uncertainty_evidence.py:22`)
   283	across a member's clock stamps. When it does not, the predicate at
   284	`joulewise/uncertainty_evidence.py:367` refuses the member with the detail
   285	string `wall_minus_monotonic_span_exceeded`.
   286	
   287	Two consecutive window-C collection attempts on 2026-07-26 failed on exactly
   288	that, and on nothing else:
   289	
   290	| Attempt | Member that failed | Observed span | Implied rate |
   291	|---|---|---:|---:|
   292	| 1 | `p2015-df-cmp-abba-ph-decode-b02-b2` | 5.544 ms | about +110 ppm |
   293	| 2 | `neg8-refcorpus-r11` | 7.769 ms | about −158 ppm |
   294	
   295	Rates of that size are what `adjtime(2)` produces. `adjtime(2)` is the system
   296	call network time synchronisation uses to correct the wall clock by speeding
   297	it up or slowing it down by a fraction of a percent, instead of jumping it, so
   298	that time keeps increasing. The evidence shows a **slew** — a gradual change
   299	of rate — and not a demonstrated discrete step: no timestamp ever moved
   300	backward, and the native powermetrics second counter advanced only by 0 or 1
   301	whole seconds. A step hidden inside the roughly 44-second gap between stamps
   302	cannot be categorically excluded.
   303	
   304	Two things are unknown and must be written as unknown wherever this is
   305	reported:
   306	
   307	- **The responsible process is unknown.** `joulewise/environment.py:908`
   308	  assigns `clock_sync.status = "limited_without_admin"` unconditionally, and
   309	  the `timed_running` field only reports whether `pgrep` found the process.
   310	  Every member, passing and failing alike, reported `timed_running=true`. The
   311	  macOS `timed` daemon is therefore **plausible but unproven**; attributing it
   312	  would require privileged inspection of the unified log.
   313	- **The correlation with time of day is noted but unproven.** Window B had
   314	  zero occurrences across 59 members, collected 23:57–03:15 local. Window C
   315	  ran roughly 7% per member — 2 occurrences across about 30 members, collected
   316	  03:17–05:19 local. Do not assert a nightly maintenance-window cause.
   317	
   318	What is established: only a privileged wall-clock adjuster can produce this.
   319	Ordinary sampling load, thermal state, and CPU activity cannot move the wall
   320	clock relative to the monotonic clock. The excursion also self-clears — member
   321	`neg8-refcorpus-r12`, collected immediately after the failing `r11`, anchored
   322	cleanly with a 0.305 ms span.
   323	
   324	### Before the window (administrator rights required)
   325	
   326	macOS gates both the read and the write of this setting behind administrator
   327	rights (`systemsetup -getusingnetworktime` and
   328	`systemsetup -setusingnetworktime`), so the chain script can neither perform
   329	nor verify this step. Ed performs it by hand.
   330	
   331	- [ ] **Confirm the system clock is actually correct first.** Disabling
   332	  automatic time on a wrong clock freezes that error in place for the whole
   333	  window. Compare the system clock against an independent trusted source and
   334	  correct it before going further.
   335	- [ ] Record the current setting so it can be restored:
   336	
   337	  ```sh
   338	  sudo systemsetup -getusingnetworktime
   339	  ```
   340	
   341	- [ ] Disable automatic network time adjustment:
   342	
   343	  ```sh
   344	  sudo systemsetup -setusingnetworktime off
   345	  ```
   346	
   347	- [ ] Settle 150–240 seconds — use 180 — after this administrator action, as
   348	  after any other operator activity, before launching the chain.
   349	- [ ] After the window closes, meaning after `measurement_complete`, the
   350	  whole-window verdict, and the backup, re-enable it:
   351	
   352	  ```sh
   353	  sudo systemsetup -setusingnetworktime on
   354	  ```
   355	
   356	- [ ] Record in the close-out that automatic time was disabled, when it was
   357	  disabled, and when it was restored.
   358	
   359	Leaving automatic time off is not a protocol state. It is a temporary machine
   360	condition the operator owns for one window, and the close-out must show it was

   103

   107

   109

   111	
   112	### Frozen operational thresholds
   113	
   114	These values are already defined, but the final chain must consume the issued artifact mechanically rather than trusting copied literals:
   115	
   116	| Gate | Required result |
   117	|---|---|
   118	| Wall-versus-monotonic span | No more than `0.005 s` per member. |
   119	| Pre-calibration fiducial | `b_fiducial_s <= 0.033558756679900`. |

   121	| Budgetable ordinary excess | At most `0.001275166090593858 s`, for maximum drift `0.012093166090593858 s`; identified systematic defects are never budgeted. |
   122	| Bound freshness | Minted from all 12 bound members inside this window; maximum age `86400 s`; exact OS, supply, and calibration identities must match. |
   123	| Environment | AC and externally connected, low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, screensaver disengaged, thermal pressure nominal. |
   124	| CPU admission | At least 30 samples; busy-ratio p95 no more than `0.5`; combined processor power p95 no more than `1.0 W`. |
   125	| Stage failure behavior | `--max-failures 1`; only a preregistered recovery may relaunch a stage. |
   250	  Evidence: final timestamp in `window-chain.log`.
   251	
   252	### Automatic stop rules
   253	
   254	- [ ] A display wake, screensaver engagement, CPU-admission failure, operator touch, or unknown environment state loses the affected occurrence. Never use an environment override.
   255	
   256	- [ ] A member-level clock-anchor failure is preserved and quarantined; there is no member-level anchor retry.
   257	
   258	- [ ] A pre-calibration level failure ends the attempt before member 1. Relaunch only after a named cause was removed and only within the frozen cause-removal retry count.
   259

   261	
   262	- [ ] The third failure on the same cause closes the window.

I’m validating the secondary failure modes now, especially whether failed/partial POST attempts can be repaired and whether bracket selection can accidentally borrow another window’s receipt.

  6036	def _axi_strict_reason_codes(problems: Sequence[str]) -> list[str]:
  6037	    """Project strict validator diagnostics onto its frozen reason enum."""
  6038	
  6039	    codes = {
  6040	        problem.split(":", 2)[1]
  6041	        for problem in problems
  6042	        if problem.startswith("axi:") and len(problem.split(":", 2)) == 3
  6043	    }
  6044	    unknown = sorted(codes - AXI_VALIDATOR_REASON_CODES)
  6045	    if unknown:
  6046	        raise ValueError(
  6047	            "strict validator returned reason codes outside "
  6048	            f"AXI_VALIDATOR_REASON_CODES: {unknown}"
  6049	        )
  6050	    if problems and not codes:
  6051	        raise ValueError(
  6052	            "strict-invalid AXI bundle produced no AXI_VALIDATOR_REASON_CODES value"
  6053	        )
  6054	    return sorted(codes)
